docs.title: ZenSynora Architecture
docs.text:
Status: reflects v0.7.5 (2026-10-14). Updated from the v0.4.1 version: adds the Web UI settings API, provider routing changes, the safe updater and the doctor/medic rewrite (0.7.0); chat channels, agent-to-agent events, jobs, backups, model rotation, custom providers and approval-gated self-update (0.7.1); test inventory recounted. Unreleased: Telegram bot fixed and able to run inside the Web UI (web/telegram_api.py). Audience: contributors and operators. For end-user docs see README.md. Sprint history: archive/SPRINTS_SUMMARY.md.

This document is a high-level map of the codebase and how the modules fit together. It complements docs/architecture_diagram.md (visual flow) by explaining why each layer exists.

docs.title: 2. Request lifecycle
docs.text:
The "happy path" for a single user message:

channel (web chat / telegram / whatsapp / cli)
  telegram only: allowFrom check → per-chat queue → worker → @agent routing
  → Agent.think()
      → _route_message()      task timer, guardrails, model selection,
                              medic loop guard (working since 0.7.0)
      → _build_context()      memory + knowledge retrieval
      → _provider_chat()      LLM call (provider.py)
                              ─ semantic_cache lookup
                              ─ retry/backoff, circuit breaker
                              ─ offline fallback to another local provider
                                (never the one that just failed) [0.5.0]
                              ─ retry without tools if the server rejects them
                              ─ metrics (logged on failure since Sprint 1)
      → _execute_tools()      parallel + sequential tool dispatch
      → _handle_summarization() background memory cleanup
  ← response string
channel sends reply (Telegram: split into ≤ 4096-character messages)

The Telegram bot runs either inside zensynora webui (started by web/telegram_api.py when channels.telegram.run_in_webui is on) or in zensynora gateway (gateway.py) — never both, because Telegram allows only one copy of a bot to receive updates.

docs.title: Where Sprint 2-4 modules plug in
docs.text:
• observability.span("agent.think", ...) — wrap any of the steps above to get distributed traces. The decorator/context-manager is a no-op when the OTel SDK isn't installed, so wrapping is free.
  • resilience.FallbackChain — wrap _provider_chat in a chain of providers; failed providers get their own CircuitBreaker so the next request isn't slowed down by a flapping endpoint. (Wiring is up to the operator — the framework now ships the building blocks.)
  • structured_output.repair_json — used by Agent.complete_structured() to coerce free-form LLM responses into Pydantic-validated payloads, with one or more LLM-driven repair rounds on failure.
  • prompts.PromptRegistry — agent profiles can be promoted from hard-coded strings to versioned, JSONL-backed templates. Future sprints will route _load_system_prompt through this.
  • vector.make_backend("qdrant", ...) — knowledge.db's BM25 search can be paired with semantic search by populating a VectorBackend alongside it. The choice of backend is a config string.

docs.title: myclaw/observability/
docs.text:
• init_tracing(...) — idempotent global setup; reads ZENSYNORA_TRACING_ENABLED.
  • @traced / @traced_async — decorators; no-op when disabled.
  • with span("name", **attrs): — context manager; no-op when disabled.
  • Optional dep: opentelemetry-sdk (python -m pip install 'zensynora[tracing]').

docs.title: myclaw/resilience/
docs.text:
• CircuitBreaker(name, failure_threshold, reset_timeout, ...) — async-safe. Three states: CLOSED → OPEN → HALF_OPEN. excluded_exceptions lets you exempt user-input errors that shouldn't trip the breaker.
  • FallbackChain([(name, async_fn), ...]) — each provider gets its own breaker; OPEN providers are skipped without invocation.

docs.title: myclaw/logging_config.py (Sprint 2 additions)
docs.text:
• PIIScrubFilter — redacts emails, phones, API keys, JWTs from log messages, args, and extra_fields. User IDs hashed to user:<sha256[:10]>.
  • Default-on; opt out with MYCLAW_LOG_SCRUB_PII=false.
  • myclaw/logging.py is deprecated as of 2026-05-18 — delegates to this module.

docs.title: myclaw/http_session.py + myclaw/aiohttp_session.py (2026-05-17)
docs.text:
• http_session.py — shared requests.Session singleton for sync HTTP with connection pooling and TCP keep-alive.
  • aiohttp_session.py — shared aiohttp.ClientSession singleton for async HTTP with connection pooling. Lazily created, auto-closed at exit.
  • Both modules reduce latency for frequent outbound calls (web search, MCP HTTP transport, knowledge fetching).

docs.title: myclaw/tools/browser.py
docs.text:
• Playwright-backed: browser_navigate, browser_screenshot, browser_fill_form, browser_extract_text, browser_wait_for, browser_close_session.
  • Persistent contexts keyed by session_id; module-level pool capped at 10.
  • Optional dep: playwright (python -m pip install 'zensynora[browser]').
  • Returns {"ok": False, "error": "..."} if Playwright isn't installed — no crash.

docs.title: myclaw/prompts/
docs.text:
• PromptTemplate — name, version, body, description, tags, variables.
  • PromptRegistry — append-only JSONL at ~/.myclaw/prompts.jsonl.
  • register() auto-increments version; get(name) returns latest.
  • Jinja2 when available; string.Template fallback otherwise.

docs.title: myclaw/structured_output/
docs.text:
• extract_json(text) — pulls first balanced JSON object/array out of free-form text; handles code fences, prose wrappers, nested braces, quoted strings.
  • validate_json(text, schema) — schema may be a Pydantic v2 model (preferred) or a JSON-schema dict.
  • repair_json(text, schema, llm_call, max_attempts=1) — provider-agnostic.
  • Agent.complete_structured(messages, schema, ...) wraps it.

docs.title: myclaw/vector/ (Sprint 4)
docs.text:
• VectorBackend — abstract async interface: upsert, search, delete, count, clear.
  • InMemoryBackend — zero-dep, brute-force cosine. Tests + tiny corpora.
  • SQLiteBackend — JSON blob storage + Python cosine. Persistent, no new deps. Good up to ~10–50 K vectors.
  • QdrantBackend — production HNSW. Optional dep (python -m pip install 'zensynora[qdrant]'). Run locally with docker run -p 6333:6333 qdrant/qdrant.
  • make_backend(name, config) — config-driven factory; falls back to SQLite if Qdrant requested but client missing.

docs.title: webui/src/components/CostDashboard.tsx
docs.text:
• Self-contained React component; no external chart library.
  • Fetches /api/v1/costs/{summary,by-provider,by-model,timeline} (all added in Sprint 3) and refreshes every 60 s.

docs.title: 4. Optional dependency posture
docs.text:
Install optional packages into the activated project virtual environment; see the README installation guide. Do not run these commands against Debian/Ubuntu system Python (PEP 668).

Every advanced feature with an external dep degrades gracefully:

Since 0.5.0 the openai SDK is a core dependency: llama.cpp, LM Studio, OpenAI, Groq and OpenRouter all need it, and a missing SDK used to make chat silently fall back to Ollama.

Feature Optional package Without it... Anthropic / Gemini providers anthropic / google-generativeai Provider raises a clear ProviderUnavailableError; the doctor and Settings → Test connection report it Tracing opentelemetry-sdk All tracing helpers no-op Browser tools playwright Tools return structured errors Jinja2 templates jinja2 Falls back to string.Template JSON-schema dicts jsonschema Pass Pydantic models instead Qdrant qdrant-client Factory falls back to SQLite JWT verification PyJWT[crypto] First .verify() raises RuntimeError OAuth token exchange httpx (core dep, present) n/a Discord channel discord.py DiscordChannel.run() raises RuntimeError

Install all extras: python -m pip install 'zensynora[all]'.

docs.title: 5. Outstanding deferrals
docs.text:
• agent_internals explicit-DI refactor — Sprint 5 extracted the three big phases as free functions; Sprint 9 wrapped them in classes (MessageRouter, ContextBuilder, ToolExecutor, ResponseHandler) but those classes still take an agent reference. Next iteration: replace with explicit per-dependency constructor args (timer, memory provider, hooks). See docs/dev/DECOMPOSITION_PLAN.md.
  • Slack channel adapter — [slack] extra reserved; adapter not yet built.
  • LoRA adapter loader + training-data exporter — net-new feature; tracked.
  • Removing the embedded literal in myclaw/agents/registry.py — once the YAML format has been stable across one minor release; the sync invariant test catches drift in the meantime.

docs.title: 7. Where to look next
docs.text:
• Add a new tool → CONTRIBUTING.md walkthrough; tools go in myclaw/tools/ and are auto-discovered.
  • Add a new LLM provider → subclass the appropriate base in provider.py; update the factory in the same file.
  • Add a new vector backend → subclass VectorBackend in myclaw/vector/, then teach factory.make_backend about its name.
  • Add a new channel → match the pattern in channels/telegram.py (access check, per-chat queue and workers, dispatch into Agent.think).
  • Add a health check → one @check function in myclaw/doctor/checks.py (guide).
  • Change the data format → add a migration in updater/migrations/ (guide).
  • Change how updates work → add a Step in updater/steps.py.
  • Add a Web UI page → a component in webui/src/components/, a NavButton in App.tsx, a router in myclaw/web/ included in api.py.
  • Emit agent activity → myclaw.events.emit({"type": …}) from code that runs for an agent; it reaches the channel automatically.
  • Add a provider preset → PROVIDER_PRESETS in myclaw/web/settings_api.py.

docs.title: Medic Agent Change Management Enhancement
docs.text: Applies to: v0.7.0 · Reviewed: 2026-10-13. Change management is a Python API (myclaw.agents), not an LLM tool. Since 0.7.0 the log analyzer reads ~/.myclaw/logs/zensynora.log, which ZenSynora now writes by default — earlier versions wrote no log file, so the analyzer had nothing to read. User-facing health checks are in the Medic & Doctor Guide.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The Medic Agent has been enhanced with comprehensive change management capabilities. These features enable the agent to:

  1. Continuously monitor logs from all relevant sources
  2. Detect anomalies and failures automatically
  3. Create change plans with proper documentation
  4. Manage approval workflow for changes
  5. Execute changes safely with rollback capability
  6. Maintain audit history of all changes
  7. Escalate to humans when needed

docs.title: New Files
docs.text:
1. myclaw/agents/medic_change_mgmt.py (900+ lines)
  2. ChangeManagementSystem - Core change management logic
  3. ChangeStatus, ChangePriority, ChangeType - Enums for change classification
  4. ChangePlan - TypedDict for change plan structure
  5. LogAnalyzer - Log ingestion and anomaly detection
  6. ScheduledReviewSystem - Automated review scheduling
  7. Convenience functions for CLI/tool integration

docs.title: Modified Files
docs.text:
1. myclaw/agents/__init__.py
  2. Exported new change management classes and functions

docs.title: 1. Change Plan Creation
docs.text:
from myclaw.agents import create_change_plan, ChangeType, ChangePriority

result = await create_change_plan(
    title="Fix memory leak in agent.py",
    description="Patch to address memory leak issue",
    rationale="Detected in logs - memory usage increasing over time",
    change_type="patch",  # config, code, security, patch, hotfix
    priority="high",      # critical, high, medium, low
    affected_components=["myclaw/agent.py"],
    proposed_changes={"myclaw/agent.py": "new content here"},
    risks=["May break existing functionality"],
    rollback_steps=["Restore from backup"]
)

docs.title: 2. Approval Workflow
docs.text:
• Auto-approval for low-risk configuration changes (configurable)
  • Manual approval required for code changes, security changes, high/critical priority
  • Audit trail of all approvals with timestamps and approver identity
from myclaw.agents import approve_change

result = await approve_change("CHG_20250111_120000_abc123", approved_by="operator")

docs.title: 3. Safe Execution with Rollback
docs.text:
from myclaw.agents import execute_change

# Dry run first
result = await execute_change("CHG_20250111_120000_abc123", dry_run=True)

# Execute for real
result = await execute_change("CHG_20250111_120000_abc123", dry_run=False)
# Automatically creates backups and rolls back on failure

docs.title: 4. Log Analysis and Anomaly Detection
docs.text:
from myclaw.agents import analyze_system_logs

# Analyze logs from last 60 minutes
report = analyze_system_logs(since_minutes=60)
print(report)

Anomaly patterns detected: - ERROR, CRITICAL, FATAL messages - Exceptions and Tracebacks - Timeout errors - Connection refused - Permission denied - Disk full / memory errors - Segmentation faults

docs.title: 5. Continuous Monitoring
docs.text:
from myclaw.agents import start_continuous_monitoring, stop_continuous_monitoring

# Start automated reviews every 60 minutes
start_continuous_monitoring()

# Stop monitoring
stop_continuous_monitoring()

When anomalies are detected: 1. Automatically creates a change plan 2. Auto-approves if low-risk 3. Executes the change 4. Logs everything to audit trail

docs.title: 6. Pending Changes Management
docs.text:
from myclaw.agents import get_pending_changes, get_change_history

# View pending approvals
print(get_pending_changes())

# View change history
print(get_change_history(limit=10))

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The change management system can be configured via:

  • auto_approve_low_risk - Auto-approve low priority patches/hotfixes
  • auto_approve_config - Auto-approve configuration changes
  • maintenance_window_start/end - Restrict changes to maintenance windows
  • review_interval_minutes - How often to run scheduled reviews

docs.title: Integration with Tools
docs.text:
The new functions can be registered as tools for the agent:

from myclaw.tools import register_tool
from myclaw.agents import (
    create_change_plan, approve_change, execute_change,
    analyze_system_logs, get_pending_changes
)

# Register as available tools
register_tool("create_change_plan", create_change_plan)
register_tool("approve_change", approve_change)
register_tool("execute_change", execute_change)
register_tool("analyze_logs", analyze_system_logs)
register_tool("get_pending_changes", get_pending_changes)

docs.title: Security Features
docs.text:
1. Least privilege - Changes are made with minimal required access
  2. Audit trail - Every action logged with timestamp and identity
  3. Backup before change - Automatic backups enable rollback
  4. Approval workflow - Human oversight for high-risk changes
  5. Maintenance windows - Restrict changes to approved windows
  6. Dry-run capability - Test changes before applying

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• Failed changes automatically trigger rollback
  • All errors logged to audit trail
  • Notifications sent for failures requiring human intervention
  • Graceful degradation when components are unavailable

docs.title: Manual Change Workflow
docs.text:
import asyncio
from myclaw.agents import (
    create_change_plan, approve_change, execute_change,
    get_pending_changes
)

async def manual_fix():
    # 1. Create change plan
    result = await create_change_plan(
        title="Update config timeout",
        description="Increase timeout from 30s to 60s",
        rationale="Users experiencing timeouts on slow connections",
        change_type="config",
        priority="medium",
        affected_components=["config.py"],
        proposed_changes={"config.py": "TIMEOUT = 60"}
    )
    print(result)

    # 2. Check pending (if not auto-approved)
    print(get_pending_changes())

    # 3. Approve if needed
    await approve_change("CHG_20250111_120000_abc123", "admin")

    # 4. Execute
    result = await execute_change("CHG_20250111_120000_abc123")
    print(result)

asyncio.run(manual_fix())

from myclaw.agent import Agent

docs.title: Updating ZenSynora safely
docs.text:
ZenSynora updates side by side: the new version is downloaded and built in its own folder while the current one keeps working. It is only switched in after it has passed its checks against your configuration. Before anything changes, your data and the whole installed program folder are backed up; any failure puts the previous version back exactly as it was.

Updated for v0.7.1: full program-folder backup and restore, settings/API keys/knowledge base checked and restored after the switch, approval-gated self-update proposals (see Medic & Doctor).

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
From the Web UI (v0.7.4): open Updates (or click the version at the bottom of the sidebar). Check for updates compares the installed version with GitHub; Update now runs the same safe update described below and shows each step and the log while it runs (it keeps going if you close the page); Roll back returns to the previous version. When it is done, click Restart ZenSynora — the server restarts with the new version and the page reloads by itself. Branch or tag and Reinstall even if up to date match --ref and --force below. Updating from the Web UI needs a standard install (~/.local/share/zensynora); it is available from this computer or with the admin key, like Settings.

From a terminal:

zensynora update                  # update to the latest version (GitHub main)
zensynora update status --check   # what's installed, is a newer version out?
zensynora update rollback         # go back to the previous version

If the zensynora command isn't available, use the script directly: bash ~/.local/share/zensynora/source/update.sh (same options).

Command What it does update (default) Update to the latest main. --ref v0.7.1 for a tag/branch, --from-dir PATH / --from-archive FILE for offline updates, --run-tests to run the test suite before switching, --force to reinstall the same version, --app-backup full\|code\|none for the program-folder backup (default full; code skips venv/). rollback Activate the previous version. Restores ~/.myclaw too only if that update changed your data (--restore-data / --keep-data to override). --to RELEASE picks a specific one. status [--check] [--json] Installed version, available releases and backups, recent updates. backup [--label X] Back up ~/.myclaw now (for selective backups use zensynora backup create or the Web UI Backups page). restore --backup NAME Restore ~/.myclaw from a backup (current data is saved first). prune Delete old releases/backups (defaults: keep 3 releases, 5 backups).

After an update, restart ZenSynora if it was running: click Restart now in the Web UI banner, or stop zensynora webui (Ctrl+C) and start it again. A terminal opened before the update still points at the old version — since 0.7.2 commands started there switch to the installed version by themselves, and the Web UI shows a banner while an older server is still running. Reload the browser page afterwards.

Upgrading from an install made before 0.6.0 (no update.sh yet): run the online installer once — it detects the existing install and runs the updater:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adrianx26/zensynora/main/install-online.sh | bash

docs.title: What happens during an update
docs.text:
1 preflight        Python ≥ 3.11, ~1.5 GB free, find current version, service running?
 2 fetch            download/copy new source → releases/<version>-<time>/
 3 handoff          if the new version ships a newer updater, it takes over
 4 backup data      ~/.myclaw + .env + data/ → backups/<time>-<from>-to-<to>/  (mode 700)
 5 backup program   the whole running release folder (code, venv, web UI, .env,
                    your own files) → app-folder.tar.gz + an inventory of every file
 6 carry-over       copy .env and data/ into the new release
 7 build            new venv, requirements, `pip install -e`, your extra packages, web UI
 8 verify           imports, load YOUR config with the new code, `zensynora --help`
 9 stop service     systemd `myclaw` (only if it was running)
10 migrate          versioned data migrations (see below)
11 activate         atomically repoint  source -> releases/<new>
12 restore data     settings, API keys and knowledge base checked; anything missing
                    is put back from the backup of step 4
13 start service    and confirm it stays up
14 finalize         record history, prune old releases/backups

Steps 1–10 never touch the running version. If any step fails, the completed steps are undone in reverse order: the new release folder is deleted, data is restored from the backup if a migration ran, source is pointed back, the service is restarted — and the previous program folder is compared with the inventory from step 5 and restored from the archive if anything in it differs (changed, missing or extra files). The update log says what was restored.

Program-folder archives are large (about the size of the folder, compressed), so they are kept for the last two updates; data backups follow --keep-backups (default 5). Backups you make yourself (update.sh backup, zensynora backup, the Web UI) are never pruned automatically.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
~/.local/share/zensynora/
  source -> releases/0.6.0-20261013T203000   # what everything runs from
  releases/                                  # one complete copy per version (own venv)
  backups/                                   # data snapshots + program archives (contain API keys)
  staging/                                   # temporary copies for approved self-update proposals
  logs/update-*.log                          # full log of every update
  updater-state.json                         # history used by rollback
~/.myclaw/                                   # your data, shared by all versions
  .migrations.json                           # which data migrations have run

Paths through source/ (systemd unit, source/venv/bin/activate) keep working across updates because source is a symlink. The first update of an older in-place install moves it to releases/<version>-legacy-… so it stays available for rollback.

Docker deployments update by rebuilding the image (install.sh --docker); data lives in the Docker volume and is not touched by this updater. Back it up first with the Web UI Backups page or docker compose exec zensynora zensynora backup create.

docs.title: Changes proposed by agents
docs.text: Agents can propose changes to ZenSynora's own code. An approved proposal is installed by this updater exactly like an update from a local folder (--from-dir a copy of the current release with the change applied, --force), so every safeguard above applies, and rollback undoes it. Details: Medic & Doctor → Self-update proposals.

docs.title: For developers: extending the update procedure
docs.text: The updater (updater/) uses only the Python standard library, so it runs even when the app's own environment is broken.

docs.title: Add a data migration
docs.text:
When a release changes the format of anything in ~/.myclaw (config keys, database schema, folder layout), add updater/migrations/m_NNNN_name.py:

ID = "0002_rename_provider_key"          # unique, sortable, never reused
DESCRIPTION = "Rename providers.llama -> providers.llamacpp"
REVERSIBLE = False                       # informational

def apply(ctx):                          # ctx.data_dir, ctx.app_version, ctx.log
    cfg = ctx.data_dir / "config.json"
    ...                                  # must be safe to run more than once

Migrations run once each, in ID order, inside the new release's environment (so they may import myclaw), after the backup and before the switch. A failing migration aborts the update and the backup is restored. Fresh installs record all current migrations as applied (install.sh runs python -m updater migrate).

docs.title: Add or change an update step
docs.text: Steps live in updater/steps.py; each is a class with run(ctx) and rollback(ctx), and the order is default_pipeline(). To add behaviour (e.g. "pull a new Ollama model"), write a Step, make its rollback undo it, and insert it in the list. Context carries everything steps share.

docs.title: Change the updater itself
docs.text: Users run the updater of the version they have installed. If a newer release needs different update logic, bump UPDATER_PROTOCOL in updater/__init__.py; older updaters then hand over to the newly downloaded one before doing anything else.

docs.title: Test
docs.text: tests/test_updater.py covers the pipeline rollback, backups, migrations, adoption of legacy installs, version policy and pruning without network access; tests/test_selfupdate.py covers proposals going through it. For an end-to-end check, point --base/--data-dir at a scratch folder and update between two local source trees with --from-dir.

docs.text: Applies to: v0.7.1 · Reviewed: 2026-10-13. v0.7.1: delegation works again (before, every delegate call answered "Agent registry not initialized"), and in the Web UI each hand-over between agents — delegation or swarm — is shown in the chat channel and its Activity panel (Web UI guide). docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Agent Swarms is a powerful multi-agent coordination system for MyClaw that enables multiple AI agents to collaborate on complex tasks. Instead of relying on a single agent, swarms distribute work across specialized agents using various coordination strategies.

docs.title: 🏗️ Agent Swarm Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    UI["USER INTERFACE<br/>(CLI, Telegram, WhatsApp, API)"] --> Orchestrator["SWARM ORCHESTRATOR<br/>(Central Controller)"]

    Orchestrator --- Ops["Create Swarms | Execute Tasks | Monitor Status"]

    Orchestrator --> Strategies

    subgraph Strategies ["COORDINATION STRATEGIES"]
        direction LR
        Parallel["PARALLEL<br/>(Simultaneous)"]
        Sequential["SEQUENTIAL<br/>(Pipeline)"]
        Hierarchical["HIERARCHICAL<br/>(Managed)"]
        Voting["VOTING<br/>(Consensus)"]
    end

    Strategies --> Aggregator["AGGREGATION ENGINE<br/>(Consensus | Best Pick | Synthesis)"]
    Aggregator --> Result["SWARM RESULT"]

docs.title: 🎯 Swarm Coordinator (Hierarchical Strategy)
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Coord["Coordinator (lead_dev)"] --> Plan["1. Analyze Task & Plan"]
    Plan --> Delegate["2. Delegate to Workers"]

    subgraph Workers ["Specialized Workers"]
        W1["Security Expert"]
        W2["Performance Reviewer"]
        W3["Style Checker"]
    end

    Delegate --> W1 & W2 & W3
    W1 & W2 & W3 --> Synthesize["3. Synthesize Results"]
    Synthesize --> Final["Final Coherent Report"]

docs.title: Agent Swarm Components
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph Config ["Configuration"]
        direction TB
        C1["name"]
        C2["strategy"]
        C3["workers"]
        C4["coordinator"]
    end

    subgraph Task ["Task Execution"]
        direction TB
        T1["description"]
        T2["input_data"]
        T3["status"]
    end

    Config & Task --> Orchestrator["SWARM ORCHESTRATOR"]
    Orchestrator --> Engine["AGGREGATION ENGINE"]
    Engine --> SResult["SWARM RESULT<br/>(Confidence, Time, Data)"]

docs.title: Data Flow Diagram
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant UI as CLI/Telegram/WhatsApp
    participant Orchestrator
    participant Storage as SQLite (swarm.db)
    participant Agents as Agent Registry
    participant Engine as Aggregator

    User->>UI: Task Request
    UI->>Orchestrator: swarm_assign(swarm_id, task)
    Orchestrator->>Storage: Load Swarm Config
    Orchestrator->>Agents: Initialize Workers

    rect rgb(200, 220, 240)
        Note over Orchestrator, Agents: Strategy Execution (Parallel/Sequential/...)
        Orchestrator->>Agents: Execute sub-tasks
        Agents-->>Orchestrator: Individual results
    end

    Orchestrator->>Engine: Aggregate results
    Engine-->>Orchestrator: Final result
    Orchestrator->>Storage: Save execution history
    Orchestrator-->>User: Return Swarm Result

docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> PENDING: Created by User
    PENDING --> RUNNING: Execution Started
    RUNNING --> COMPLETED: Success Result
    RUNNING --> FAILED: Error Occurred
    RUNNING --> TERMINATED: User Stopped
    FAILED --> [*]
    COMPLETED --> [*]
    TERMINATED --> [*]

swarm_create(
    name="architecture_vote",
    strategy="voting",
    workers="architect1,architect2,architect3,architect4",
    aggregation="consensus"
)

swarm_assign(
    swarm_id="swarm_vote123",
    task="Should we use microservices or monolith?"
)
# Consensus determines the winning approach

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Add to your ~/.myclaw/config.json:

{
  "swarm": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max_concurrent_swarms": 3,
    "default_strategy": "parallel",
    "default_aggregation": "synthesis",
    "timeout_seconds": 300,
    "swarm_memory_limit": 50
  }
}

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text: Option Default Description enabled true Enable/disable swarm functionality max_concurrent_swarms 3 Maximum parallel swarms per user default_strategy "parallel" Default execution strategy default_aggregation "synthesis" Default result aggregation timeout_seconds 300 Maximum execution time swarm_memory_limit 50 Max messages stored per swarm

docs.title: Use Case 1: Research Team (Parallel)
docs.text:
Goal: Get multiple perspectives on a research topic

swarm_create(
    name="ai_impact_research",
    strategy="parallel",
    workers="tech_analyst,market_researcher,ethics_reviewer",
    aggregation="synthesis"
)

swarm_assign(
    swarm_id="swarm_xxx",
    task="Analyze the impact of AI on healthcare in 2024"
)

Result: Combined insights from technical, market, and ethical perspectives

docs.title: Use Case 2: Content Pipeline (Sequential)
docs.text:
Goal: Create polished content through multiple stages

swarm_create(
    name="technical_blog_pipeline",
    strategy="sequential",
    workers="topic_researcher,outline_writer,content_writer,editor,seo_optimizer",
    aggregation="concatenation"
)

swarm_assign(
    swarm_id="swarm_xxx",
    task="Create a comprehensive guide on async/await in Python"
)

Flow: Research → Outline → Draft → Edit → SEO Optimize

docs.title: Use Case 3: Code Review with Coordinator (Hierarchical)
docs.text:
Goal: Thorough multi-aspect code review

swarm_create(
    name="comprehensive_code_review",
    strategy="hierarchical",
    coordinator="senior_architect",
    workers="security_specialist,performance_engineer,style_reviewer",
    aggregation="synthesis"
)

swarm_assign(
    swarm_id="swarm_xxx",
    task="Review this authentication microservice"
)

Process: 1. Senior architect analyzes and creates review plan 2. Specialists review their assigned aspects 3. Architect synthesizes findings into actionable report

swarm_create(

docs.title: 1. Agent Selection
docs.text:
Complementary Skills: - Research team: researcher1, researcher2, researcher3 (different specialties) - Code review: security_expert, performance_reviewer, style_checker - Content: researcher, writer, editor

Coordinator Selection: - Should have good planning capabilities - Needs to understand the big picture - Prefer models with strong reasoning

docs.title: 2. Strategy Selection Guide
docs.text: Task Type Strategy Why Research/Broad Analysis Parallel Multiple perspectives simultaneously Content Creation Sequential Progressive refinement Complex Multi-part Tasks Hierarchical Orchestrated subtasks Decision Making Voting Consensus validation Code Review Parallel or Hierarchical Different aspects or orchestrated Data Processing Sequential Step-by-step transformation

docs.title: 3. Aggregation Selection
docs.text: Goal Method Example Get diverse perspectives Concatenation Research reports Find best single answer Best Pick Code solutions Quick agreement Consensus Yes/No decisions Comprehensive summary Synthesis Final reports

docs.title: 4. Resource Management
docs.text:
# Check current usage
swarm_stats()

# Clean up old swarms
swarm_list(status="completed")  # Find completed
swarm_terminate("swarm_old123")  # Clean up

docs.title: swarm_create()
docs.text:
Create a new swarm.

Parameters: - name (str): Descriptive name for the swarm - strategy (str): One of: parallel, sequential, hierarchical, voting - workers (str): Comma-separated list of agent names - coordinator (str, optional): Coordinator agent name (required for hierarchical) - aggregation (str): One of: consensus, best_pick, concatenation, synthesis - user_id (str, optional): User identifier

Returns: Swarm ID (e.g., swarm_abc123def456)

docs.title: swarm_assign()
docs.text:
Execute a task with the swarm.

Parameters: - swarm_id (str): Swarm identifier - task (str): Task description/prompt - user_id (str, optional): User identifier

Returns: Formatted results including: - Individual agent outputs - Confidence score - Execution time - Aggregated final result

docs.title: swarm_status()
docs.text:
Get current swarm status.

Parameters: - swarm_id (str): Swarm identifier

Returns: Status information (pending, running, completed, failed, terminated)

docs.title: swarm_result()
docs.text:
Get detailed execution result.

Parameters: - swarm_id (str): Swarm identifier

Returns: Complete result with individual agent outputs

docs.title: swarm_terminate()
docs.text:
Force stop a running swarm.

Parameters: - swarm_id (str): Swarm identifier

docs.title: swarm_list()
docs.text:
List all swarms.

Parameters: - status (str, optional): Filter by status - user_id (str, optional): User identifier

docs.title: swarm_stats()
docs.text:
Get usage statistics.

Parameters: - user_id (str, optional): User identifier

Returns: Statistics including counts, avg confidence, execution times

docs.title: "Maximum concurrent swarms reached"
docs.text:
Cause: Hit the max_concurrent_swarms limit

Solutions: 1. Wait for existing swarms to complete 2. Terminate unused swarms: 

swarm_list(status="running")
swarm_terminate("swarm_xxx")
3. Increase limit in config: 
{"swarm": {"max_concurrent_swarms": 5}}

docs.title: "Agent not found in registry"
docs.text:
Cause: Agent name doesn't exist in the agent registry

Solution: Check available agents and correct the name: 

# List available agents
# (Check your config.json agents.named section)

docs.title: Swarm execution timeout
docs.text:
Cause: Task took longer than timeout_seconds

Solutions: - Break task into smaller parts - Increase timeout in config - Use fewer workers for faster execution

docs.title: Low confidence scores
docs.text:
Cause: Agents disagree significantly or quality varies

Solutions: - Try different aggregation method - Provide clearer, more specific task description - Add more workers (for voting strategy) - Use coordinator for better synthesis

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: Swarm data is stored in ~/.myclaw/swarm.db:

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
swarms - Swarm configurations and status - Strategy, workers, coordinator settings

swarm_tasks - Individual task assignments - Input/output data

swarm_messages - Inter-agent communication log - Useful for debugging

swarm_results - Execution results - Individual and aggregated outputs

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text:
Old swarms are automatically cleaned up after 30 days. You can manually clean up:

# In Python code
from myclaw.swarm import SwarmStorage
storage = SwarmStorage()
deleted = storage.cleanup_old_swarms(days=7)
print(f"Cleaned up {deleted} old swarms")

docs.title: Custom Strategies
docs.text:
You can extend the system with custom strategies by inheriting from BaseStrategy:

from myclaw.swarm.strategies import BaseStrategy

class MyCustomStrategy(BaseStrategy):
    async def execute(self, task, workers, coordinator=None):
        # Your custom logic here
        pass

docs.title: Direct Orchestrator Access
docs.text:
For programmatic control:

from myclaw.swarm import SwarmOrchestrator, SwarmConfig, SwarmStrategy

orchestrator = SwarmOrchestrator(agent_registry, config)

# Create swarm
config = SwarmConfig(
    name="my_swarm",
    strategy=SwarmStrategy.PARALLEL,
    workers=["agent1", "agent2"]
)
swarm_id = await orchestrator.create_swarm(config)

# Execute and get result object directly
result = await orchestrator.execute_task(swarm_id, "My task")
print(result.confidence_score)
print(result.individual_results)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Agent Swarms enable powerful multi-agent collaboration through:

  1. Four Strategies - Parallel, Sequential, Hierarchical, Voting
  2. Flexible Aggregation - Combine results intelligently
  3. Coordinator Role - For complex orchestrated tasks
  4. Persistent Storage - Track and analyze swarm operations
  5. Easy Integration - Works with all existing MyClaw features

Start simple with Parallel strategy, then explore Hierarchical with a Coordinator for complex workflow

docs.title: 3. A chat message, end to end
docs.text:
What happens inside one agent when it answers (Telegram and the terminal follow the same path from Agent onwards; the Telegram steps before Agent are in §15). Since 0.7.1 the Web UI reaches Agent.stream_think through chat channels — see §12; the per-agent socket shown here still works for scripts.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as You
    participant UI as Web UI (React)
    participant WS as web/api.py<br/>WebSocket /ws/chat/{agent}
    participant A as Agent.stream_think
    participant R as router + medic loop guard
    participant C as context_builder
    participant M as memory.py
    participant K as knowledge/
    participant P as provider.py
    participant T as tools/

    U->>UI: type a message
    UI->>WS: send text
    WS->>WS: quota + optional MFA check
    WS->>A: stream_think(text, user="webui")
    A->>R: start task timer, depth + loop limits
    A->>M: add(user message)
    A->>C: build context
    C->>M: get_history() (flushes buffered turns)
    C->>K: search notes for relevant knowledge
    C-->>A: system prompt + history + knowledge
    A->>P: chat(messages, stream=True)
    P-->>A: token stream (+ tool calls, collected at the end)
    A-->>WS: tokens
    opt no text and no tool calls (empty reply)
        A->>P: ask once more without streaming
        P-->>A: reply, or "model returned an empty answer" note
    end
    WS-->>UI: __STREAM_START__ … tokens … __STREAM_END__
    opt the model asked for tools
        A->>T: execute (parallel when independent)
        T-->>A: results
        A->>P: chat again with tool results
        P-->>A: final answer stream
        A-->>WS: tokens
    end
    A->>M: add(assistant reply)
    UI-->>U: rendered reply

docs.title: 4. Provider selection, rotation and fallback
docs.text:
How a request reaches a model, and what happens when that fails. Changed in 0.5.0: the agent never silently switches to another provider unless you asked for it — 0.7.1 adds an explicit rotation list (Models page).

flowchart TD
    start(["Agent needs a reply"]) --> rot{"Rotation on and this agent<br/>uses the default model?"}
    rot -- yes --> order["Candidates = default + rotation list<br/>(round-robin: start at the next one)"]
    order --> tryc["provider.chat() with candidate"]
    tryc -- ok --> replied(["Stream reply<br/>(model shown on the message)"])
    tryc -- "error: rate limit, down,<br/>missing model, in-stream error" --> nextc{"more candidates?"}
    nextc -- yes --> tryc
    nextc -- no --> fail(["Error shown in chat"])
    rot -- no --> pick["Provider = agent's own, else agents.defaults.provider<br/>(built-in or one of your providers)"]
    pick --> init{"Provider can start?<br/>(SDK installed, API key set)"}
    init -- no --> err["ProviderUnavailableError<br/>clear message shown in chat"]
    init -- yes --> breaker{"Circuit breaker<br/>open?"}
    breaker -- closed --> llmcall["provider.chat()"]
    llmcall -- ok --> replied
    llmcall -- "server rejects tool list<br/>(llama.cpp without --jinja)" --> notools["Retry once without tools<br/>remember for next calls"]
    notools --> replied
    llmcall -- "connection error" --> offline{"intelligence.offline_mode?"}
    breaker -- open --> offline
    offline -- no --> fail
    offline -- yes --> fb["Try local providers in order<br/>Ollama → LM Studio → llama.cpp<br/>(skipping the one that just failed)"]
    fb -- ok --> replied
    fb -- none reachable --> fail
Provider Talks to Python package llamacpp llama-server (OpenAI API, default :8080/v1) openai ollama Ollama native API (:11434/api/chat) — (httpx) lmstudio LM Studio (OpenAI API, :1234/v1) openai openai, groq, openrouter OpenAI-compatible cloud APIs openai anthropic Anthropic Messages API anthropic (optional) gemini Google Gemini google-generativeai (optional) your own (providers.custom) any OpenAI-compatible server, or another Ollama openai / httpx

docs.title: 5. Tool execution
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    llm["Model returns tool calls"] --> exec["agent_internals/tool_executor.py"]
    exec --> indep{"Independent<br/>of each other?"}
    indep -- yes --> par["Run in parallel"]
    indep -- no --> seq["Run in order"]
    par & seq --> hooks["pre/post hooks<br/>tools/core.py"]
    hooks --> kind{"Tool type"}
    kind -- shell --> allow["Allow-list + blocked commands<br/>tools/shell.py"]
    kind -- generated / external skill --> sb["Sandbox<br/>sandbox.py · worker_pool.py"]
    kind -- web / browser --> ssrf["URL safety checks<br/>tools/web.py · tools/browser.py"]
    kind -- other --> direct["Run function"]
    allow & sb & ssrf & direct --> audit["audit_log.py · metrics"]
    audit --> back["Results back to the model"]

docs.title: 6. Swarms
docs.text:
A swarm splits one task across several agents (swarm/orchestrator.py).

flowchart LR
    task(["Task"]) --> orch["SwarmOrchestrator"]
    orch --> strat{"Strategy"}
    strat --> p["Parallel<br/>all agents at once"]
    strat --> s["Sequential<br/>each builds on the last"]
    strat --> h["Hierarchical<br/>coordinator delegates"]
    strat --> v["Voting<br/>agents vote on answers"]
    p & s & h & v --> agg["Aggregation<br/>synthesis · best · concatenate"]
    agg --> store[("swarm/storage.py<br/>SQLite")]
    agg --> result(["Result"])

docs.title: 9. Safe updates
docs.text:
zensynora update (updater/, added in 0.6.0; program-folder backup and data check added in 0.7.1). Steps 1–10 never touch the running version; any failure undoes the completed steps in reverse order.

flowchart TD
    s1["1 Preflight<br/>Python, disk space, service state"] --> s2["2 Fetch<br/>GitHub, folder or archive"]
    s2 --> s3["3 Hand-off<br/>newer updater takes over"]
    s3 --> s4["4 Back up ~/.myclaw + .env"]
    s4 --> s5["5 Back up the whole program folder<br/>archive + inventory of every file"]
    s5 --> s6["6 Carry over .env, data/"]
    s6 --> s7["7 Build side by side<br/>venv · packages · extras · Web UI"]
    s7 --> s8["8 Verify<br/>imports new code, loads YOUR config"]
    s8 --> s9["9 Stop service"]
    s9 --> s10["10 Data migrations"]
    s10 --> s11["11 Activate<br/>atomic symlink switch"]
    s11 --> s12["12 Settings, API keys, knowledge<br/>checked, restored if missing"]
    s12 --> s13["13 Start service, confirm up"]
    s13 --> s14(["14 Record, prune old releases"])

    s2 & s7 & s8 & s10 & s11 & s13 -. "failure" .-> rb["Roll back<br/>old version active again · data restored if migrated ·<br/>program folder compared with the inventory and<br/>restored from the archive if anything differs"]
