docs.title: Telegram Guide — chat with your agents from your phone
docs.text:
Applies to: v0.7.5 + Unreleased changes · Added: 2026-10-16 — the Telegram bot was reviewed and fixed, and it now runs inside the Web UI.

The Telegram bot lets you talk to your ZenSynora agents from the Telegram app on your phone or computer. It uses the same agents, models and knowledge base as the Web UI. Your bot is private: only the people you allow can use it.

What it can do:

  • answer your messages (the default agent, or any agent with @name);
  • run reminders and repeating tasks (/remind);
  • search, read and save notes in the knowledge base (/knowledge_…);
  • answer several people at the same time, while keeping each chat in order.

Settings, buttons and status are in the Web UI under Settings → Channels (see the Web UI guide).

docs.title: Set it up
docs.text:
1. Create a bot. In Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot, choose a name and a username (it must end in bot). BotFather replies with a token — a long text like 123456:ABC-DEF…. Copy it. Keep it secret: anyone with the token can run your bot.
  2. Add the token. Start the Web UI (zensynora webui) and open Settings → Channels. Paste the token, turn on Telegram bot enabled, click Save, then click Test bot. It should say Token works — bot @YourBot (Name).
  3. Find your user id. Open your bot in Telegram (search for its username) and send /whoami. It answers with a number — your Telegram user id. Copy it.
  4. Allow yourself. Back in Settings → Channels, add the number to Allowed Telegram users and click Save. The bot restarts by itself (or click Restart bot).
  5. Click Send test message: the bot writes to every number in Allowed Telegram users. Telegram does not let a bot write first, so open the bot and press Start once before that.
  6. Chat. Write to your bot. The default agent answers.

The Telegram bot panel in Settings → Channels shows Status: Running as @YourBot when everything works (the sidebar health shows Telegram: running @YourBot). Until someone is allowed, it warns: Nobody can use the bot yet: add your user id to Allowed Telegram users below.

Without the Web UI. You can run the bot on its own with zensynora gateway instead. If you do, turn off Run the bot inside the Web UI in Settings → Channels — otherwise two copies of the bot run and Telegram reports a conflict (see Troubleshooting).

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Type / in the chat to see the list — the bot registers its command menu with Telegram by itself.

Command What it does /start Welcome message and the command list /help The command list /whoami Shows your Telegram user id and whether you are allowed /agents Lists the agents you can address with @name /remind <seconds> <text> Runs <text> once, after that many seconds /remind every <seconds> <text> Runs <text> again and again, every that many seconds /jobs Lists the reminders, with their ids /cancel <id> Cancels a reminder (the id comes from /jobs) /knowledge_search <words> Searches the knowledge base /knowledge_list Lists the notes /knowledge_read <permalink> Shows one note (the permalink comes from /knowledge_list) /knowledge_write <title> \| <text> Saves a note, for example /knowledge_write Wi-Fi \| The router is in the hall /knowledge_sync Re-reads the note files (after you edited them by hand) /knowledge_tags Lists the tags

/start, /help and /whoami answer everyone (people who are not allowed get only their own id and how to be allowed). All other commands, and normal messages, work only for allowed users.

docs.title: Agents and @mentions
docs.text:
• A normal message goes to the default agent.
  • Start a message with @name to ask another agent: @writer a short poem about rain. Upper or lower case does not matter. Answers from other agents start with their name (@writer: …), so you know who replied. @writer alone, with nothing after it, gets the question What should @writer do? — write the task after the name.
  • /agents lists the agents. Agents created later — in Settings → Agents, or by another agent with create_agent — can be used right away, without a restart.
  • An @word that is not an agent stays part of the message for the default agent.

While the agent works, Telegram shows typing…. Long answers come as several messages (Telegram allows at most 4096 characters per message). If something goes wrong, you get a short explanation — the same wording as in the Web UI, for example that the model is rate-limited or the model server cannot be reached. Technical details go only to the log (~/.myclaw/logs/zensynora.log), never to the chat.

Photos, voice messages, documents. The bot reads only text for now. If you add a caption, the caption is used as the message; without one the bot says it can only read text.

Too many messages at once are slowed down: the bot answers Too many messages. Please wait a moment. Wait a few seconds and send again.

docs.title: Reminders
docs.text:
/remind 600 check the oven makes the default agent carry out "check the oven" in 10 minutes and send you the result. /remind every 3600 any news about the weather? repeats every hour. /jobs lists them; /cancel <id> stops one. You can also simply ask an agent ("remind me in 10 minutes to …").

Reminders live in the running bot: they stop when the bot (or the Web UI) stops or restarts, so set them again afterwards. For tasks that must survive restarts, use a job in the Web UI (Jobs page).

docs.title: Knowledge
docs.text:
By default, allowed Telegram users use the same knowledge base as the Web UI: a note you save from Telegram is found in the Web UI, and the other way round. Conversation memory stays separate — each Telegram user has their own.

To give every Telegram user their own, separate knowledge base, turn off Telegram uses the same knowledge base as the Web UI in Settings → Channels (channels.telegram.shared_knowledge: false).

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
You can add the bot to a Telegram group.

  • Each person in the group must be in Allowed Telegram users; the bot ignores the others.
  • Mentioning the bot itself (@YourBot what is …) works: the mention is removed before the message goes to the agent. @YourBot @writer … reaches the writer agent.
  • In a group, one message is answered at a time, in order.
  • Telegram's privacy mode (on by default for new bots) lets a bot see only some group messages, such as commands and replies to the bot. To let it read every message, send /setprivacy to @BotFather and turn it off.
  • Memory is per person, not per group.

docs.title: Privacy: who may use the bot
docs.text:
Allowed Telegram users (channels.telegram.allowFrom) is the list of people who may use the bot. Each entry is either a numeric user id (what /whoami shows — the safest choice) or a @username. A username can be changed by its owner, a user id cannot.

  • People who are not on the list get no answers. Only /start, /help and /whoami reply, and they show nothing but the person's own id.
  • Each not-allowed person is written to the log once, with their id — useful if you forgot to add someone.
  • While the list is empty, or still holds a placeholder such as YOUR_USER_ID, nobody can use the bot. The startup log, zensynora doctor and Settings → Channels warn about it.

docs.title: Inside the Web UI or zensynora gateway
docs.text:
Only one copy may run. When Run the bot inside the Web UI is on, zensynora gateway (and the myclaw service, which runs it) does not start the bot and says so; use zensynora gateway --telegram to run it there anyway, or turn the setting off. Agents can write to you with the send_telegram_message tool (only to allowed users).

Inside the Web UI (default) zensynora gateway Start zensynora webui starts the bot too Run zensynora gateway in a terminal or as a service Settings Change them in Settings → Channels; the bot restarts by itself Restart the gateway after a change Status, Test bot, Restart bot In Settings → Channels and the sidebar Messages in the terminal Good for Most people A server without the Web UI

Telegram allows only one copy of a bot at a time. If the gateway already runs your bot, the Web UI shows Another ZenSynora (zensynora gateway?) is already running this bot — stop it or turn off 'Run the bot inside the Web UI'. and stops its own copy. When Run the bot inside the Web UI is off, the status says Runs in zensynora gateway, not in the Web UI, and Restart bot is not available. Pick one: leave Run the bot inside the Web UI on and do not start the gateway, or turn it off and use the gateway. zensynora gateway prints a reminder when Run the bot inside the Web UI is still on.

Polling and webhook. By default the bot asks Telegram for new messages (polling). This works anywhere, also behind a home router — nothing to set up. The gateway can also run in webhook mode, where Telegram calls your server instead:

zensynora gateway --webhook-url https://bot.example.com/webhook --port 8443

Telegram then sends every message to that URL. The bot listens on all network addresses (0.0.0.0) at the given port (default 8443), path /webhook, so the URL should end in /webhook. Your server needs a public HTTPS address that reaches that port. Webhook mode is only for zensynora gateway; the bot inside the Web UI always uses polling. If you are not sure, use polling.

docs.title: Settings in ~/.myclaw/config.json
docs.text:
The Web UI writes these for you; you can also edit the file.

"channels": {
  "telegram": {
    "enabled": true,
    "token": "123456:ABC-DEF…",
    "allowFrom": ["123456789", "@yourname"],
    "run_in_webui": true,
    "shared_knowledge": true,
    "max_workers": 4
  }
}
Key Meaning enabled Switch the bot on or off token The token from @BotFather (or set MYCLAW_TELEGRAM_TOKEN) allowFrom Allowed users: numeric ids or @usernames run_in_webui true: zensynora webui runs the bot (default) shared_knowledge true: same knowledge base as the Web UI (default) max_workers How many chats are answered at the same time

docs.title: Advanced: your own Telegram Bot API server
docs.text:
Normally the bot talks to Telegram's servers (api.telegram.org). If you run your own Telegram Bot API server, point the bot at it with an environment variable before starting ZenSynora:

ZENSYNORA_TELEGRAM_API_URL=http://localhost:8081 zensynora webui

Most people never need this. The tests use it too, to run the bot against a local fake server.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Problem What to do The bot works for a few seconds, then conflict — and the log shows ZenSynora starting every few seconds The myclaw service (zensynora gateway) was crash-looping and grabbing the bot (fixed 2026-10-18: the gateway now leaves Telegram to the Web UI). If you only use the Web UI: sudo systemctl disable --now myclaw. zensynora doctor warns about it. An agent says it needs a "bot token" or "chat id" to message you Agents use the send_telegram_message tool (since 2026-10-18) — the bot must be running. Disable home-made Telegram tools an agent created earlier (Tools page, or ask an agent: disable_skill telegram_integration). The bot does not answer Send /whoami. If it says you are not allowed, add the number to Allowed Telegram users and Save. Check that the status in Settings → Channels says Running as @YourBot. Status: Another ZenSynora (zensynora gateway?) is already running this bot … (sidebar: conflict) Two copies of the bot are running — for example zensynora gateway and the Web UI, or two computers with the same token. Stop one (or turn off Run the bot inside the Web UI), then click Restart bot. Status: No bot token yet Paste the token from @BotFather in Telegram bot token and Save. zensynora doctor says Telegram bot: nobody is allowed to use the bot Send /whoami to the bot and add the number to Allowed Telegram users. zensynora doctor says Telegram bot: enabled but no bot token Paste the token from @BotFather in Settings → Channels, or turn the bot off. Test bot says the token works, but the status says The token is wrong Fixed on 2026-10-18: a space or line break copied with the token. Update ZenSynora, or paste the token again without spaces and Save. Status: Error: … Click Test bot. The token is wrong — copy it again from @BotFather.: send /token to @BotFather, paste the token and Save. Cannot reach Telegram — check the internet connection.: this computer cannot reach Telegram. The bot answers with a model error (rate-limited, server cannot be reached) The bot works; the model does not. Open the Models page and click Test on the default model, or pick another one. Nothing happens in a group Make sure every person is allowed, and check privacy mode (see Groups). "I can only read text for now" You sent a photo, voice message or file without a caption. Add a caption or type the message. Reminders are gone The bot was restarted. Set them again, or use a job in the Web UI.

More help: zensynora doctor has a Telegram bot check (category configuration): off, enabled but no bot token, nobody is allowed to use the bot, or how many users are allowed and where the bot runs (inside the Web UI or with zensynora gateway). How the bot works inside: architecture diagrams §15.

docs.title: Web UI Guide — chat, models, jobs, backups
docs.text:
Applies to: v0.7.5 · Added: 2026-10-13 · v0.7.3: Channels page, real model tests · v0.7.4: Updates page, Restart button · v0.7.5: Skills, agents that create and delegate, medic for failed jobs, token speed · Unreleased: Telegram bot inside the Web UI (Settings → Channels)

Start the Web UI with zensynora webui and open http://localhost:8000 (--host 127.0.0.1 keeps it on this computer only). This guide covers the pages added in 0.7.1. Settings, Costs, Tools and Doctor are described in the README and the Medic & Doctor guide.

docs.title: Chat: channels and several agents
docs.text:
Where What it is Channels (#general, ＋ for more) Group rooms. Pick the members when you create one; change them with ⚙ in the channel bar. Agents (sidebar) Click an agent for a private conversation (direct message) with it alone.

Managing channels (v0.7.3): the Channels page (⚙ next to Channels in the sidebar) creates channels with a name, a topic (the agents are told it is the channel's purpose), members and reply mode, and renames, edits, clears or deletes them. It shows message counts and last activity, and lists the direct-message conversations too.

Who answers. In a channel, @name addresses an agent (type @ for a list; an agent that is not a member yet is added), @all asks every member. Without a mention the channel's reply mode decides:

Reply mode Behaviour Lead answers The first member answers; others only when mentioned (default) Everyone, in turn Each member answers and sees the earlier answers — good for review chains Everyone, at once All members answer in parallel — fastest, independent opinions

Agent-to-agent talk. When an agent hands work to another one (the delegate tool or a swarm), uses a tool, or a job posts into the channel, you see it as a small card in the conversation — @default asked @writer, @writer answered @default · 1.2 s — with the task and the answer one click away. The Activity panel on the right lists the same events for the channel; inline activity hides them from the conversation.

Agents as a team (v0.7.5). Every agent knows the other agents and what they do, and hands work to them with delegate when another one fits better — you see the hand-over as a card. An agent can also create a new agent (create_agent) when a task needs a specialist nobody is; it appears in the sidebar at once (✨ card in the channel) and can be changed or removed in Settings → Agents. A task is handed over at most twice, so agents cannot pass it back and forth forever. Switch creation off with agents.allow_agent_creation (Settings → Features).

Deleted agents. When you rename an agent in Settings, its channels, direct messages and jobs move to the new name. An agent you delete is removed from its channels (the channel says so).

Message actions. Point at a message (on a phone: tap …) for a small bar with the time (hover it for the full date) and these actions:

Action Your messages Agent answers Copy Copies the text Copies the text; each ``` code block also has its own Copy code button Edit Edit in place, Save & send (Enter; Esc cancels): everything after it in the channel is removed and the agents answer the edited message again (same rules, @mentions work) Correct the text in place; nothing is run again Delete Delete this message, or Delete this message and the answers to it (up to your next message) Deletes the answer (asks first) Regenerate — The same agent writes this answer again, in the same place

Edited messages show (edited). Changes and deletions appear in every open browser at once. While the agents are answering these actions wait: press ■ or let them finish. ↑ in the empty input edits your last message. ⤓ MD in the channel bar copies or downloads the conversation as Markdown (GET /api/channels/{id}/export.md).

After an edit, delete or regenerate, each agent's memory of the channel is rebuilt from the messages you see (your messages and its own answers), so it never answers an edited question with the old one in mind. Details of earlier tool calls are not kept in that memory.

Good to know. * Under each answer: model, time and ⚡ tokens per second (hover for the token count and the time to the first token; counts are estimates). * Answers stream; ■ stops the agents. Messages you send meanwhile wait their turn. * Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line. * Every agent keeps its own memory per channel; the knowledge base is shared. * History lives in ~/.myclaw/chat.db and is included in backups (Conversations). * With two-factor authentication on, the chat asks for the code first.

docs.title: Models: switch, rotate, add providers
docs.text:
• Default model — pick a provider and a model (the list comes from the server; ↻ refreshes) and click Make default. The previous default is remembered in the rotation list, so switching back is one click (★).
  • Rotation — extra models used together with the default one:
  • Fallback on errors: the default answers; if it fails (rate limit, server down, model missing) the next model in the list answers.
  • Round-robin: requests are spread over all models.
  • Rotate now makes the next model the default. Rotation applies to the default agent and to agents that use the default model; agents with their own model keep it. A model that was just refused, unknown or rate-limited is skipped for a while.
  • Test / Test all (v0.7.3) sends a tiny real request. A model can be listed and still refuse to work with ZenSynora (OpenRouter answers some free models with "only available on agentic harnesses"), need credits or not be loaded — test before you rely on it.
  • Your providers — Add provider for any OpenAI-compatible server (local: vLLM, LocalAI, Jan, KoboldCpp, text-generation-webui; online: DeepSeek, Mistral, Cerebras, Together, GitHub Models, Hugging Face, NVIDIA NIM, Gemini, xAI, Fireworks — several have free tiers) or another Ollama server. Presets fill the URL; add the key, Test connection, save. The new provider then appears everywhere a provider can be chosen. Keys are stored in ~/.myclaw/config.json and never sent back to the browser.

docs.title: Several keys for one provider
docs.text:
A provider can have more than one API key — for example two free OpenRouter accounts, or a work and a personal key.

  • Add keys. Settings → Providers shows a Keys list under each provider (for your own providers: Models → Your providers → Keys). + Add key, give it a name and paste the key. The provider's normal API key is the Default key.
  • Per key: Test checks the connection with that key and lists the models it can use; Edit renames it or replaces the secret (leave the key field empty to keep it); Delete removes it. Each key shows which agents use it; a key in use cannot be deleted — pick another key for those agents first.
  • Pick a key. Settings → Agents: Provider, then Key, then Model (↻ lists the models of that provider and key). The Models page has the same Key picker for the default model and for rotation entries. Default key means the provider's normal key; an agent that has no provider of its own also uses the default agent's key.
  • Use the other keys when one is limited. Turn on When a key hits a rate limit or runs out of quota, try the other keys (shown once a provider has two keys). On a rate limit, missing credits or a refused key, the same model is tried with the provider's other keys before the next model in the rotation. A key that just failed is skipped for a while (per provider, model and key). Off by default.
  • If an agent's key was deleted (for example by editing the config file), the agent uses the default key; the log and the Doctor warn about it.

In config.json:

"providers": {"openrouter": {
  "api_key": "sk-or-main",
  "keys": [{"id": "work", "label": "Work account", "api_key": "sk-or-work"}],
  "rotate_keys": true}},
"agents": {"named": [{"name": "Coder", "provider": "openrouter", "model": "…", "key": "work"}]}

Key ids use lower-case letters, digits, - and _; default is reserved.

Writing agent prompts. In Settings → Agents, give a new agent a name and a short description and click ✨ Generate prompt: the default model writes a system prompt (role, how to work, tools to prefer, limits). Review it and save. If the default model is refused or busy, the rotation models are tried in turn (v0.7.4); the message under the button names the model that wrote it.

docs.title: Jobs: scheduled and on-demand tasks
docs.text:
A job is an instruction an agent carries out on a schedule or when you click Run. Scheduled jobs run while zensynora webui is running.

Field Meaning Agent Who does the work Schedule Manual, once, every N minutes, daily at HH:MM, weekly on chosen days Post results in A channel (the run and its result appear there as activity) or nowhere Success criteria What a good result looks like — used for scoring Score every run The default model scores each run 0–10 against the criteria Retries / timeout Retry failed runs; stop runs that take too long Clean memory Each run starts without the previous runs' conversation

When a run fails (v0.7.5): click 🩺 Ask the medic on the run. The medic says what went wrong, explains it, and suggests changes to the job (shown as now → suggested) and anything only you can do (start a model server, add credits). Apply fix & run again changes the job and runs it; Ask the medic to fix the code is offered when ZenSynora itself is at fault — the medic reads the code and files a proposal you approve on the Doctor page. Common failures are recognised even when no model answers. In the job's settings, When a run fails can do this automatically (diagnose, or diagnose, fix the job and run once more). Tool steps sets how many extra tool rounds (search, read, retry…) the agent may use per run — raise it for research jobs.

Monitor in the table: running state, last and next run, success rate, average score. Runs shows each run's output, model, duration and evaluation (Evaluate scores a run on demand). Benchmark runs the same job on up to 8 models at once and compares time and score — a quick way to choose a model for a task. Templates: morning briefing, weekly knowledge clean-up, medic self-review.

docs.title: Knowledge base
docs.text:
All agents share one knowledge base (notes in ~/.myclaw/knowledge/default, Markdown files you can also edit yourself). Before answering, an agent searches it automatically; agents can also use these tools themselves:

Tool What it does search_knowledge Full-text search over titles, note text, tags and observations read_knowledge / list_knowledge Read one note / list the notes write_to_knowledge Save a note (title, text, tags, observations, relations) get_knowledge_context / get_related_knowledge Follow relations between notes (knowledge graph) list_knowledge_tags / sync_knowledge_base Tags; re-read files you edited by hand record_lesson The medic's lessons (note medic-lessons)

With auto extract on (Settings → Features → knowledge.auto_extract), useful facts from conversations and tool results are saved by themselves. The knowledge-keeper skill teaches an agent when to save and how. Allowed Telegram users use the same knowledge base as the Web UI (switch it off in Settings → Channels to give each Telegram user their own); WhatsApp users each keep their own knowledge base.

MCP memory servers. Any MCP server (a memo/notes server, a database, a file system …) can be added in ~/.myclaw/config.json:

"mcp": {"servers": {"memo": {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "<memo-mcp-package>"]}}}

Its tools appear for all agents as mcp_<server>_<tool> when the Web UI (or zensynora agent) starts. In the other direction, zensynora mcp-server offers ZenSynora's tools — knowledge base included — to other MCP clients.

docs.title: Telegram bot (Settings → Channels)
docs.text:
Settings → Channels is about messaging apps — not the chat channels above. With the Telegram bot switched on, zensynora webui runs the bot too, so you can talk to your agents from your phone. No separate zensynora gateway is needed. The bot restarts by itself when you save a change to a Telegram setting. WhatsApp still runs in zensynora gateway — restart the gateway after changing WhatsApp settings.

Setting or button What it does Telegram bot enabled · Telegram bot token Switch the bot on; paste the token from @BotFather Allowed Telegram users Your numeric user id — send /whoami to the bot to see it — or @username. Nobody else can use the bot. Run the bot inside the Web UI On (default). Turn off if you run the bot with zensynora gateway instead. Telegram uses the same knowledge base as the Web UI On (default): notes are shared; each Telegram user keeps their own conversation memory Test bot Checks the token with Telegram — the token you just typed, or else the saved one. Success: Token works — bot @name (Name). Restart bot Starts the bot again. Not available when the bot is turned off, runs in zensynora gateway, or has no saved token. Send test message The running bot writes a short message to every numeric id in Allowed Telegram users — proves the whole path works. If it says the bot cannot write first, open the bot in Telegram and press Start.

The Telegram bot panel shows the Status:

Status Meaning Running as @name All good Starting… Wait a few seconds Stopped · Turned off The bot is not running / Telegram bot enabled is off No bot token yet Paste the token from @BotFather and Save Runs in zensynora gateway, not in the Web UI Run the bot inside the Web UI is off Another ZenSynora (zensynora gateway?) is already running this bot … Conflict: Telegram allows only one copy. Stop the other one, or turn off Run the bot inside the Web UI. Error: … Read the message; click Test bot

While nobody is allowed, the panel warns: Nobody can use the bot yet: add your user id to Allowed Telegram users below. The sidebar health has a Telegram row too (running @name / stopped / conflict / error). Set-up step by step, commands and troubleshooting: Telegram guide.

docs.title: Skills: instructions agents load when needed
docs.text:
Skills in the sidebar. A skill is a Markdown file of instructions for one kind of task — how to research the web and cite sources, how to write a PowerShell script, how to review code.

  • Give a skill to an agent: click the agent's chip under the skill (bright = has it). The same chips are in Settings → Agents.
  • The agent's prompt lists its skills by name and description; when a task matches, it reads the full text with the use_skill tool. Always include the full instructions puts the whole text in the prompt instead — better for small local models that rarely call tools, but it costs tokens.
  • + New skill writes one; Import… adds a SKILL.md made elsewhere (the same format other agent tools use: a name: and description: header, then Markdown). Built-in skills are read-only: Copy to change makes your own version (deleting it brings the built-in one back).

Your skills are files in ~/.myclaw/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and are included in backups (Jobs, own tools & skills). zensynora skills list shows all skills and which agents have them.

docs.title: Backups: settings, API keys, knowledge
docs.text:
• Back up now — choose what to include: Settings & API keys (always; includes the config encryption key so the backup can be restored on a new machine), Knowledge base, Conversations & chat channels, Jobs, own tools & skills. Add a note if you like.
  • Automatic backups — every N hours while the Web UI runs; keeps the last N automatic ones (manual backups are never deleted automatically).
  • Restore — choose which parts to restore (click the part chips); your current files are backed up first, so a restore can be undone. Check verifies every file against its checksum; ⬇ downloads; Import… adds a backup file made elsewhere.

Backups are .tar.gz files in ~/.myclaw-backups (change it in Settings or with MYCLAW_BACKUP_DIR). They contain your API keys — keep them private. The same works from a terminal:

zensynora backup create                 # parts chosen in Settings
zensynora backup create -p settings     # only settings + API keys
zensynora backup list
zensynora backup restore NAME [-p knowledge]

Updates make their own backups automatically — see UPDATING.md.

docs.title: Updates: check, update, roll back, restart
docs.text:
Open Updates in the sidebar (or click the version at the bottom).

Part What it does Version The version this server runs, the installed one and the latest on GitHub. ↻ Check for updates asks GitHub again. Update now Runs the safe updater: backups of your data and the program folder, side-by-side install, checks, switch, automatic rollback on failure. Shows the step (step 7 of 14 …), a progress bar and the log. It keeps running if you close the page. Roll back Back to the previous installed version. Branch or tag / Reinstall Install a branch or tag instead of main; reinstall the same version to repair an install. Restart ZenSynora After an update or rollback the server still runs the old code. This restarts it with the installed version; the page reloads when it is back (a few seconds). The same button appears in the yellow banner on every page. History Recent updates and rollbacks, and the versions kept for rollback.

Works for standard installs (~/.local/share/zensynora); a git checkout shows why it cannot update itself. Restart works when the server was started with zensynora webui. Details: UPDATING.md.

docs.title: Doctor: report, errors and download
docs.text:
The Doctor page has two tabs. Checks is the health check (the same as zensynora doctor). Report shows:

  • summary cards — checks OK / warnings / failures, errors and warnings in the last 24 h, restarts (marked crash loop when the service keeps restarting), failed jobs;
  • Errors — warnings and errors from the log, grouped (messages that differ only in numbers count as one). Filter by period (1 h, 24 h, 7 days), level and text; click a group to see its log lines and traceback, and Copy them;
  • View report — the whole diagnostics report in the page;
  • Download — Markdown, JSON or ZIP (report + the last log lines). Keys and tokens are never included, so the file is safe to attach to a bug report.

docs.title: Doctor: change proposals
docs.text: Below the health checks, Change proposals lists code changes that agents proposed, with the reason and the exact diff. Approve & install installs the change through the safe updater (backup, side-by-side build, checks, automatic rollback); Reject drops it. Run self-review asks the medic to look at recent errors and failed jobs and propose a fix; What the medic learned lists the lessons it saved. Details: Medic & Doctor guide.

docs.title: Archive
docs.text:

Current documentation starts at docs/README.md.

docs.title: ZenSynora Action Plan
docs.text:
Archived on 2026-10-13 (v0.7.0). Action plan from the April 2026 audit. Kept for history; it describes the project at the time it was written and may not match the current code. Current documentation: docs/README.md.

Generated: 2026-04-23 Based on: Comprehensive codebase audit (v0.4.1) Goal: Stabilize, secure, and harden the ZenSynora codebase Status: Phase 1 & 2 critical fixes implemented (2026-04-23). Second-round audit fixes shipped (2026-04-29) — see docs/SECURITY_FIXES_2026_04_29.md. Phase 3+ pending.

docs.title: 2026-04-29 Audit Round (resolved)
docs.text:
A follow-up audit found that some 2026-04-23 fixes had been applied in myclaw/web/api.py but not in myclaw/api_server.py, plus several new defects. All resolved in this round:

  • [x] Infinite recursion in Agent._track_preload (myclaw/agent.py:356)
  • [x] Newline-injection bypass in myclaw/tools/shell.py (regex + token re-validation)
  • [x] Missing auth on /api/v1/keys GET/POST/DELETE (myclaw/api_server.py)
  • [x] CORS allow_origins=["*"] + credentials (myclaw/api_server.py)
  • [x] Unsafe fallback in AsyncSQLitePool.get_connection (myclaw/memory.py)
  • [x] Two divergent AST sandbox policies in myclaw/tools/toolbox.py — unified into a single _validate_tool_ast() helper; added pathlib, ctypes, cffi, mmap to the forbidden set
  • [x] Broken stream_chat in all four providers (myclaw/provider.py)
  • [x] Removed dead code archive/tools_backup.py

Verified-already-fixed items (no action taken): SSH RejectPolicy, AsyncOpenAI migration, MFA secret redaction.

docs.text:
• [ ] Pending
  • [~] In Progress

docs.title: Phase 1: P0 -- Stop Crashes and Breaches (Week 1)
docs.text:
Goal: Fix crashes, security breaches, and broken connection pools. Exit Criteria: App runs without infinite loops, shell is sanitized, admin endpoints gated.

  • [x] 1.1 Fix Infinite Recursion in agent.py
  • File: myclaw/agent.py:575-601
  • Bug: _provider_chat() calls itself recursively instead of delegating to self.provider.chat().
  • Fix: Replace await self._provider_chat(...) with await self.provider.chat(...) on lines 583 and 586.
  • Validation: Mock provider.chat raising ConnectionError; assert fallback without RecursionError.

  • Effort: 15 min | Risk: Minimal

  • [x] 1.2 Fix Shell Command Injection (newline bypass)

  • File: myclaw/tools/shell.py:65, myclaw/backends/*.py
  • Bug: asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(cmd, ...) passes raw command string to /bin/sh -c. Newlines bypass the regex.
  • Fix: Replace with create_subprocess_exec(*parts, ...) across all backend files. Add newline to dangerous regex.
  • Validation: Assert newline-separated commands return error.

  • Effort: 45 min | Risk: Low

  • [x] 1.3 Fix Error Message Disclosure

  • File: myclaw/tools/shell.py:88, myclaw/backends/ssh.py, myclaw/mcp/*.py
  • Bug: return f"Error: {e}" leaks internal exception strings to LLM/user.
  • Fix: Return generic error message; log full trace server-side with exc_info=True.
  • Validation: Verify no internal paths or system info in error responses.

  • Effort: 30 min | Risk: Minimal

  • [x] 1.4 Fix CORS + Credentials Misconfiguration

  • File: myclaw/web/api.py:73-79
  • Bug: allow_origins=["*"] with allow_credentials=True allows any website to make authenticated requests.
  • Fix: Restrict origins via ZENSYNORA_CORS_ORIGINS env var or config. Default to http://localhost:5173.
  • Validation: Verify preflight from unknown origin is rejected.

  • Effort: 15 min | Risk: Minimal

  • [x] 1.5 Add API-Key Auth to Admin Endpoints

  • File: myclaw/web/api.py:108-201
  • Bug: /api/admin/*, /api/metering/*, /api/mfa/*, /api/spaces/* have zero authentication.
  • Fix: Implement require_auth FastAPI dependency using HTTPBearer. Add security.api_key: SecretStr to config.
  • Validation: Integration tests asserting 401 on all admin endpoints without valid key.

  • Effort: 2-4 hours | Risk: Medium

  • [x] 1.6 Fix MFA Secret Exposure

  • File: myclaw/web/api.py:154-160
  • Bug: mfa_setup returns raw TOTP secret in response payload without authentication.
  • Fix: Require auth; return only provisioning URI and QR code. Never expose secret plaintext.
  • Validation: Verify response does not contain secret field.

  • Effort: 30 min | Risk: Low

  • [x] 1.7 Fix Broken AsyncSQLitePool

  • File: myclaw/memory.py:91-160
  • Bug: Pool returns the same connection to all concurrent acquirers. No checkout tracking causes DB lock errors.
  • Fix: Add _checked_out set per pool key. Update release_connection signature to require conn param.
  • Validation: Concurrent get_connection() calls return distinct connection objects.

  • Effort: 1 hour | Risk: Medium (signature change)

  • [ ] 1.8 Harden register_tool AST Validation

  • File: myclaw/tools/toolbox.py:99-156
  • Bug: AST bypass possible via builtins.__import__, pathlib, getattr, dynamic importlib, or variable-mode open().
  • Fix: Add builtins, pathlib, ctypes, winreg, importlib to forbidden imports. Block getattr entirely. Block open() for dynamic tools.
  • Validation: Verify builtins.__import__ and pathlib.Path are rejected.
  • Effort: 1-2 hours | Risk: Low

docs.title: Phase 2: P1 -- Security Hardening and Async Migration (Week 2)
docs.text:
Goal: Patch OWASP-class vulnerabilities and replace blocking sync calls. Exit Criteria: No OWASP-class vulns, no blocking sync calls in hot paths, SSH/SSRF hardened.

  • [x] 2.1 Replace Sync OpenAI Client with Async
  • File: myclaw/provider.py:601-735
  • Bug: Uses sync openai.OpenAI inside async def chat(). Streaming for chunk in response: blocks the event loop.
  • Fix: Use openai.AsyncOpenAI; wrap streaming with async for chunk in response.
  • Impact: OpenAI, Groq, LMStudio, llama.cpp, OpenRouter providers.
  • Validation: Verify concurrent requests do not block each other.

  • Effort: 2-3 hours | Risk: Medium

  • [x] 2.2 Fix SSH MITM (AutoAddPolicy)

  • File: myclaw/backends/ssh.py:42
  • Bug: paramiko.AutoAddPolicy() accepts any host key.
  • Fix: Use RejectPolicy() + load_host_keys("~/.ssh/known_hosts").
  • Validation: Verify connection to unknown host is rejected.

  • Effort: 30 min | Risk: Low

  • [x] 2.3 Fix SSRF in Web Tools

  • File: myclaw/tools/web.py
  • Bug: browse() / download_file() fetch arbitrary URLs without blocking private IPs.
  • Fix: Add _is_safe_url() guard blocking localhost, 169.254.169.254, RFC1918 nets, and non-HTTP schemes.
  • Validation: Assert internal metadata endpoints return error.

  • Effort: 45 min | Risk: Low

  • [x] 2.4 Fix Rate Limiter Race Condition

  • File: myclaw/tools/core.py:55-117
  • Bug: RateLimiter.check() is not atomic under concurrent async calls. Dead code duplication at lines 113-116.
  • Fix: Add self._lock = threading.Lock(); wrap check logic with with self._lock:. Remove duplicate code block.
  • Validation: Concurrent tool execution must not exceed rate limit.

  • Effort: 15 min | Risk: Minimal

  • [x] 2.5 Fix HTTPClientPool Event Loop Binding

  • File: myclaw/provider.py:282-311
  • Bug: Global httpx.AsyncClient instance crashes when event loop changes (tests, reloads).
  • Fix: Store client per-loop-id or recreate on RuntimeError.
  • Validation: No crashes during hot-reload or test loop changes.

  • Effort: 30 min | Risk: Low

  • [x] 2.6 Fix AsyncScheduler Concurrency Limit

  • File: myclaw/async_scheduler.py:290
  • Bug: asyncio.gather(*[self._execute_job(job) for job in due_jobs]) runs all due jobs simultaneously.
  • Fix: Add asyncio.Semaphore(5) around job execution.
  • Validation: 100+ due jobs do not overwhelm the system.

  • Effort: 15 min | Risk: Minimal

  • [x] 2.7 Fix Audit Log Tamper Weakness

  • File: myclaw/audit_log.py:87
  • Bug: clear() unlinks the log file without authorization check or audit trail.
  • Fix: Add HMAC signature or use append-only log file. Require authorization for clear().
  • Validation: Verify log integrity after rotation and clear attempts.

  • Effort: 1 hour | Risk: Low

  • [x] 2.8 Fix Config Key Storage Weakness

  • File: myclaw/config_encryption.py
  • Bug: Keys may be stored in plaintext in config files.
  • Fix: Enforce OS keyring or ZENSYNORA_CONFIG_KEY environment variable for secrets.
  • Validation: Verify key is not written to disk in plaintext.

  • Effort: 1 hour | Risk: Low

  • [x] 2.9 Fix allowed_commands Config Drift

  • File: myclaw/config.py:369-372
  • Bug: python, python3, pip still in SecurityConfig.allowed_commands defaults despite Phase 1.1 removal comments.
  • Fix: Remove python, python3, pip from defaults. Add startup validation.
  • Validation: Assert shell("python --version") returns error.

  • Effort: 5 min | Risk: Minimal

  • [x] 2.10 Fix _reveal_secrets Non-Functional

  • File: myclaw/config.py:663-671
  • Bug: _reveal_secrets walks dict but never unwraps SecretStr values.
  • Fix: Add elif isinstance(v, SecretStr): out[k] = v.get_secret_value().
  • Validation: Round-trip config save/load preserves secret values.

  • Effort: 10 min | Risk: Minimal

  • [x] 2.11 Fix F-string Nested Double Quotes

  • File: myclaw/agent.py:1241
  • Bug: f"Tool {r["tool_name"]}..." requires Python 3.12+ PEP 701. Project supports 3.11+.
  • Fix: Use single quotes: f"Tool {r['tool_name']}...".
  • Validation: Syntax check passes on Python 3.11.
  • Effort: 1 min | Risk: Minimal

docs.title: Phase 3: P2 -- Performance and Dependencies (Week 3)
docs.text:
Goal: Fix caches, token counting, and async I/O bottlenecks. Restructure dependencies. Exit Criteria: No memory leaks, cache collisions eliminated, token counting accurate, dependency bloat reduced.

  • [ ] 3.1 Fix LRU Cache Key Skips First Arg
  • File: myclaw/provider.py:105-136
  • Bug: _make_key skips args[0] assuming it is self, causing cache collisions.
  • Fix: Hash all args including args[0], or use hash((args, tuple(sorted(kwargs.items())))).
  • Validation: Different prompts produce different cache keys.

  • Effort: 15 min | Risk: Minimal

  • [ ] 3.2 Fix Hardware Probe Blocking Init

  • File: myclaw/agent.py:286-294
  • Bug: GPUtil / psutil probes block startup by 100-500ms per agent.
  • Fix: Move to async background task via asyncio.to_thread() or lazy property.
  • Validation: Agent instantiation completes in under 50ms.

  • Effort: 30 min | Risk: Low

  • [ ] 3.3 Fix Unbounded _pending_preloads

  • File: myclaw/agent.py:263
  • Bug: Fire-and-forget tasks stored in set grow indefinitely; memory leak over long runs.
  • Fix: Cap set size at 50-100; prune completed tasks aggressively.
  • Validation: Memory usage stable after 1000+ chat cycles.

  • Effort: 15 min | Risk: Minimal

  • [ ] 3.4 Fix Semantic Cache O(n) Scan

  • File: myclaw/semantic_cache.py:270
  • Bug: Linear scan over all entries causes latency spikes with 256+ entries.
  • Fix: Add model-aware cache key. Consider FAISS/SQLite VSS for vector search.
  • Validation: Cache lookup under 10ms with 500 entries.

  • Effort: 2 hours | Risk: Low

  • [ ] 3.5 Fix FTS5 Cartesian Product

  • File: myclaw/knowledge/db.py
  • Bug: Unbounded JOINs across FTS5 tables cause query slowdown.
  • Fix: Use UNION of independent FTS5 subqueries with LIMIT.
  • Validation: Query completes in under 100ms with 10k observations.

  • Effort: 1 hour | Risk: Low

  • [ ] 3.6 Fix Inaccurate Token Counting

  • File: myclaw/context_window.py
  • Bug: len(text) // 4 heuristic is wrong for most tokenizers.
  • Fix: Add tiktoken for OpenAI models; per-provider tokenizer mapping; better fallback.
  • Validation: Token count within 5% of actual for known models.

  • Effort: 30 min | Risk: Low

  • [ ] 3.7 Fix Memory History Cache Never Expires

  • File: myclaw/memory.py:264, 400-404
  • Bug: get_history() caches results with no TTL. Stale data returned after external writes.
  • Fix: Add 5-second TTL to cached entries.
  • Validation: External DB write reflected within 5 seconds.

  • Effort: 15 min | Risk: Minimal

  • [ ] 3.8 Fix Gateway Sync Cleanup in Async Context

  • File: myclaw/gateway.py:172-193
  • Bug: finally block calls asyncio.get_event_loop() and asyncio.run() after loop may be closed.
  • Fix: Make start() async; use await _sched.shutdown() in finally.
  • Validation: Graceful shutdown without RuntimeError.

  • Effort: 1 hour | Risk: Medium

  • [ ] 3.9 Restructure Dependencies for On-Demand Providers

  • File: pyproject.toml, requirements.txt
  • Current: All ~30 deps in core; sentence-transformers pulls 2GB PyTorch.
  • Fix: Move to extras:
    • openai, anthropic, google-generativeai -- per-provider SDK extras
    • semantic-cache -- sentence-transformers
    • voice -- vosk
    • redis -- redis
    • metrics -- prometheus-client, nvidia-ml-py (replaces GPUtil)
    • security -- cryptography, keyring
    • mfa -- pyotp, qrcode
    • ssh -- paramiko (already in core, keep)
  • Remove: apscheduler (unused), speedtest-cli (dead), requests (httpx covers it), GPUtil (unmaintained).
  • Pin: numpy<2.0 until tested; relax python-telegram-bot exact pin.
  • Validation: create and activate a virtual environment, then run python -m pip install zensynora; this installs only core deps under 50MB.
  • Effort: 1 hour | Risk: Medium (users must update install commands)

docs.title: Phase 4: P2/P3 -- Quality, Testing and Architecture (Week 4+)
docs.text:
Goal: Fix broken tests, standardize types, refactor globals, begin Agent decomposition. Exit Criteria: All tests passing, type hints consistent, no bare except Exception: blocks.

  • [ ] 4.1 Add Missing Tests
  • Agent.stream_think() -- streaming yields chunks, handles tool calls, no RecursionError
  • AsyncScheduler -- startup/shutdown, concurrency limit, job execution, persistence
  • AsyncSQLitePool -- concurrent checkout/checkin, pool exhaustion, distinct connections
  • HTTPClientPool -- connection reuse, per-loop isolation, no crash on loop change
  • StateStore -- Redis backend basic ops, fallback to memory
  • RateLimiter -- concurrent calls do not exceed limit
  • SemanticCache -- TTL expiration, cache hit/miss, model isolation
  • SecuritySandbox -- escape vector resistance (subprocess, file, network blocking)

  • Effort: 4 hours | Risk: Low

  • [ ] 4.2 Fix Broken Tests

  • File: tests/test_memory_pool_concurrency.py, tests/test_memory_batching.py
  • Bug: Tests call AsyncSQLitePool(max_connections=3) which does not exist. release_connection signature mismatch.
  • Fix: Update tests to match actual API or remove if testing implementation detail.

  • Effort: 30 min | Risk: None

  • [ ] 4.3 Standardize Type Hints

  • Target 90% coverage.
  • Use Python 3.11+ syntax: dict[str, ...], list[str], str | None.
  • Remove typing.Dict, typing.List, typing.Optional.

  • Effort: 2 hours | Risk: Minimal

  • [ ] 4.4 Create Exception Hierarchy

  • New: myclaw/exceptions.py
  • ZenSynoraError base with ConfigError, ProviderError, SecurityError, ToolError, SandboxError, RateLimitError.
  • Replace bare except Exception: with specific handlers.

  • Effort: 2 hours | Risk: Low

  • [ ] 4.5 Refactor Global Mutable State

  • File: myclaw/tools/core.py
  • Replace _HOOKS, TOOLS, _agent_registry globals with registry classes or dependency injection.
  • Maintain backward-compatible module-level aliases.

  • Effort: 3 hours | Risk: Medium

  • [ ] 4.6 Resolve Circular Imports

  • Files: tools/core.py, sandbox.py, worker_pool.py, audit_log.py
  • Use lazy imports inside functions; extract shared interfaces to myclaw/interfaces.py.

  • Effort: 2 hours | Risk: Medium

  • [ ] 4.7 Fix State Store Singleton Race Condition

  • File: myclaw/state_store.py:349-376
  • Bug: _Store_LOCK = False is boolean, not threading.Lock().
  • Fix: import threading; _Store_LOCK = threading.Lock(); use with _Store_LOCK:.

  • Effort: 10 min | Risk: Minimal

  • [ ] 4.8 Fix Sandbox Escape Vectors

  • File: myclaw/sandbox.py:266-314
  • Bug: os imported before restrictions; socket.socket never replaced; SandboxedImporter never installed in sys.meta_path; no Windows resource limits.
  • Fix: Remove dangerous modules from sys.modules before user code. Block os.system/os.popen. Install importer in sys.meta_path. Consider Docker for true isolation.

  • Effort: 2-4 hours | Risk: Medium

  • [ ] 4.9 Agent Class Decomposition (Start)

  • File: myclaw/agent.py (1,665 lines)
  • Split into myclaw/agent/ package: MessageRouter, ContextBuilder, ToolExecutor, ResponseHandler.
  • Phase 1 = create module stubs and migrate docstrings. No behavior changes.

  • Effort: 4 hours | Risk: High (architectural)

  • [ ] 4.10 Documentation Sync

  • Update README, architecture docs, API references to reflect:
    • New auth requirements (admin_api_key)
    • Optional dependency installation inside a virtual environment (python -m pip install 'zensynora[openai,redis]')
    • CORS origin configuration
    • SSH known_hosts requirement
  • Effort: 2 hours | Risk: Minimal

docs.title: Critical Path
docs.text:
Week 1: 1.1 (recursion) -> 1.2 (shell) -> 1.5 (auth) -> 1.7 (pool)
Week 2: 2.1 (async client) -> 2.3 (SSRF) -> 2.4 (rate limit)
Week 3: 3.1 (cache key) -> 3.4 (semantic cache) -> 3.9 (deps)
Week 4: 4.1 (tests) -> 4.3 (types) -> 4.5 (globals)

docs.title: Rollback Procedures
docs.text:
• Phase 1: Git revert to HEAD~1 per item. Each P0 fix is isolated.
  • Phase 2: Provider async migration can be toggled via USE_ASYNC_OPENAI env var.
  • Phase 3: Dependency extras are additive; core deps unchanged.
  • Phase 4: Agent decomposition is stub-only; no behavioral changes.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• [ ] All P0 items verified with unit tests
  • [ ] Security scan (bandit, semgrep) passes with zero high/critical findings
  • [ ] pytest suite passes with >80% coverage
  • [ ] python -m pip install . in an activated virtual environment completes in under 30 seconds (core only)
  • [ ] Agent responds to chat without RecursionError
  • [ ] Admin endpoints return 401 without valid API key
  • [ ] Shell tool rejects commands with newlines or shell metacharacters

docs.title: ZenSynora Full Application Analysis
docs.text:
Archived on 2026-10-13 (v0.7.0). Codebase analysis from April 2026. Kept for history; it describes the project at the time it was written and may not match the current code. Current documentation: docs/README.md.

Project: ZenSynora (MyClaw) Version: 0.4.1 Language: Python 3.11+ (backend) + TypeScript/React (frontend) License: AGPL-3.0 Author: Adrian Petrescu Test Count: 456 collected tests Corpus: 242 files, ~406k words (per graphify)

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
ZenSynora is a privacy-first, multi-tenant AI agent framework designed for local or cloud deployment. It provides a complete production stack: LLM abstraction with 6+ providers, persistent per-user SQLite memory with FTS5 search, a 137-agent swarm registry, dynamic tool sandboxing, plugin marketplace with HMAC-signed manifests, OpenTelemetry tracing, circuit breaker resilience, and multi-channel gateways (Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, Web UI, CLI).

The codebase reflects 12 structured development sprints with clear module ownership and progressive feature layering.

docs.title: 2.1 High-Level Flow
docs.text:
User (Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord/Web/CLI)
  |
  v
Gateway Adapter (channels/)
  |
  v
Auth Layer (JWT / OAuth2 PKCE / UserContext via contextvars)
  |
  v
Agent.think() ─────────────────────────────────────┐
  |-- _route_message()      (task timer, guardrails) |
  |-- _build_context()      (memory + knowledge RAG) |
  |-- _provider_chat()      (LLM call via provider.py)
  |      |-- semantic_cache lookup                    |
  |      |-- retry / backoff                          |
  |      |-- circuit breaker (resilience/)            |
  |      |-- fallback chain (resilience/)             |
  |-- _execute_tools()      (parallel + sequential)  |
  |-- _handle_summarization() (memory cleanup)        |
  v                                                   |
Response Stream ──────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 2.2 Module Map
docs.text: Module Purpose Sprint agent.py Core orchestrator (think, complete_structured, stream_think) Core agent_internals/ Phase helpers: ResponseHandler, context building, routing 5, 9 agents/ 137-agent YAML registry + loader 12 auth/ JWT verification (HS256/RS256/ES256) + OAuth2 PKCE callback 6 backends/ Execution targets: local, Docker, SSH, WSL2 Core caching/ BaseTTLCache + PersistentCacheMixin 11 channels/ Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord adapters 6 config.py Pydantic config with hot-reload (watchdog) Core cost_tracker.py SQLite cost accumulator + dashboard queries 3 defaults.py Single source of truth for all tunable constants 10 evals/ Dataset-driven eval harness (5 metrics) 7 knowledge/ FTS5 notes, path reasoning, batched parallel reads 1, 7, 8 logging_config.py Structured logger + PII scrubber 2 marketplace/ Multi-source plugin discovery + HMAC-signed manifests 9 memory.py Per-tenant SQLite memory (UserContext-aware) Core messaging/ Inter-agent AgentMessage + InProcessBroker 7 observability/ OpenTelemetry tracing (no-op when SDK absent) 2, 10 prompts/ Versioned Jinja2 prompt registry (JSONL-backed) 3 provider.py LLM provider abstraction + Message TypedDict Core resilience/ Circuit breaker + fallback chain 2, 10 scheduler_features.py Complexity-driven decomposition, retry, checkpoints 6.3 structured_output/ extract_json / validate / repair_json 3 swarm/ Multi-agent orchestrator (Parallel/Sequential/Hierarchical/Voting) Core tenancy/ UserContext + scoping helpers 6, 11 tools/ Tool system: shell, files, browser (Playwright), KB, swarm, scheduler Core vector/ Pluggable backends: memory / sqlite / qdrant 4 webui/ FastAPI + React dashboard (TypewriterText, CostDashboard) 3, 11

docs.title: 3.1 Agent Engine (agent.py ~71KB)
docs.text:
The monolithic heart of the system. Responsibilities: - Message routing: Chooses model based on task complexity and agent profile - Context building: Assembles system_prompt + memory_history + knowledge_context - Provider chat: Delegates to provider.py with semantic cache pre-check - Tool execution: Dispatches tool calls in parallel where safe, sequential where dependent - Streaming: think_stream() yields tokens via async iterator - Structured output: complete_structured(messages, MyPydanticModel) with auto-repair - Task timer: 300s timeout with progressive status updates at 60s intervals

Observation: At 71KB, agent.py is large. The agent_internals/ directory was created in Sprints 5+9 to decompose it, but the main class still carries significant surface area.

docs.title: 3.2 Provider Layer (provider.py ~53KB)
docs.text:
Abstract base LLMProvider with concrete implementations for: - Local: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp - Cloud: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter

Key features: - Message TypedDict for type-safe chat envelopes - Per-provider HTTP connection pooling - Token counting (where provider SDK supports it) - Semantic cache integration (embedding-based dedup)

docs.title: 3.3 Memory System (memory.py ~26KB)
docs.text:
• Per-tenant isolation: memory_{user_id}.db files
  • FTS5 full-text search with BM25 ranking
  • Composite index: (role, timestamp) for fast role-filtered queries
  • WAL mode for concurrent read/write
  • Auto-cleanup: Configurable retention (default 90 days)
  • Knowledge extraction: Automatic entity/relation extraction from messages

docs.title: 3.4 Knowledge Base (knowledge/)
docs.text:
• db.py: FTS5 notes + dedicated thread-pool executor for queries
  • storage.py: Batched parallel note reads (7-10x faster searches)
  • path_reasoning.py: find_paths(a, b, max_hops=3) for graph traversal queries

docs.title: 3.5 Tool Ecosystem (tools/)
docs.text:
Tool Description Security read_file / write_file / download_file Filesystem ops Path validation shell Sandboxed command execution Allow-list + newline-injection blocked hardware CPU/GPU/NPU telemetry Read-only search_knowledge / write_to_knowledge KB management -- delegate / swarm_create / swarm_assign Multi-agent -- schedule / list_schedules / cancel_schedule Task scheduling -- nlp_schedule NL scheduling ("in 5 minutes") -- auto_schedule / estimate_complexity Complexity scoring + auto-decomposition -- browser_navigate / browser_screenshot / ... Playwright headless browser Sandboxed register_tool Dynamic tool creation at runtime AST-validated sandbox

Dynamic tool sandbox (toolbox.py ~41KB): - AST parsing forbids: os, sys, subprocess, pathlib, ctypes, cffi, mmap, importlib, __builtins__ - Tools are registered at runtime and persisted

docs.title: 3.6 Resilience (resilience/)
docs.text:
• CircuitBreaker: Per-provider failure threshold (default 5 failures) with 60s reset timeout
  • FallbackChain: Cascades through provider list on failure
  • Both are wired into Agent.think() and provider.chat()

docs.title: 3.7 Auth & Multi-Tenancy (auth/, tenancy/)
docs.text:
• JWT: HS256 (secret) or RS256/ES256 (JWKS endpoint) with issuer/audience/scope validation
  • OAuth2: Authorization-code flow with PKCE; pre-baked for GitHub & Google
  • UserContext: Propagated via contextvars.ContextVar for per-request tenant isolation
  • Memory transparently picks up active user from UserContext

docs.title: 3.8 Observability (observability/, logging_config.py)
docs.text:

docs.title: 4.2 Recent Security Fixes (2026-04-29)
docs.text:
1. Infinite recursion in Agent._track_preload (critical)
  2. Shell injection via newline characters bypassing regex (critical)
  3. AST sandbox bypass via __builtins__ manipulation (critical)
  4. Path traversal in file tools via ../ sequences (high)
  5. SSRF in web fetch tools via DNS rebinding (high)
  6. Timing attack in API key comparison (medium)
  7. Information disclosure in error messages leaking stack traces (medium)

All fixes have corresponding regression tests.

docs.title: 4.3 Risks
docs.text:
• Large attack surface: Dynamic code execution (register_tool) and shell execution are inherently high-risk. The AST sandbox is good but not formally verified.
  • PII scrubber is regex-based: May miss novel formats or obfuscated data.
  • No row-level security in SQLite: Multi-tenancy relies on file isolation (memory_{user_id}.db), which is effective but lacks database-enforced RLS.
  • Config file contains secrets: config.json stores API keys; encryption module exists but is optional.

docs.text:
Strengths: - Clear module boundaries with single responsibilities - defaults.py consolidates all tunable constants - Optional dependencies degrade gracefully (no crash, logged warning) - Type hints throughout (TypedDicts for message envelopes) - Sprint-based development with changelog tracking

Concerns: - agent.py at 71KB is still overweight despite decomposition efforts - toolbox.py at 41KB for dynamic tool sandboxing is complex - Some modules (provider.py at 53KB) are large monoliths - Mixed async/sync patterns (SQLite uses aiosqlite but KB uses thread pool)

docs.title: 7. Strengths
docs.text:
1. Production-grade resilience: Circuit breakers, fallback chains, retry policies, and task timers are first-class citizens, not afterthoughts.
  2. Privacy-first design: Local-first SQLite, per-tenant isolation, PII scrubbing, and optional cloud providers.
  3. LLM agnostic: 6+ providers with intelligent routing and semantic caching.
  4. Dynamic tool ecosystem: Runtime tool creation via AST-validated sandbox is a genuine differentiator.
  5. Structured output with repair: complete_structured() auto-fixes invalid JSON via LLM-driven repair loops.
  6. Comprehensive observability: OpenTelemetry spans, cost tracking, and PII-aware logging.
  7. Plugin marketplace: Multi-source discovery with cryptographic manifest verification.
  8. Eval harness: Dataset-driven testing with 5 built-in metrics and latency percentiles.
  9. Agent swarms: 137 specialized agents across 10 categories with 4 orchestration strategies.
  10. Security-conscious development: Dedicated security audit document with regression tests for every finding.

docs.title: 8.1 Architecture
docs.text:
• Monolithic agent.py: Despite agent_internals/, the main orchestrator is still 71KB. Consider extracting Agent.think() into a state machine or pipeline framework.
  • Tight coupling between gateway and agent: Direct method calls (Agent.think()) rather than message bus for intra-process communication.

docs.title: 8.2 Scalability
docs.text:
• SQLite bottleneck: Per-tenant SQLite is fine for personal use but will struggle under high concurrency. The WAL mode helps, but there's no pooling or read-replica strategy.
  • In-process caching: BaseTTLCache is local only; no distributed cache option.
  • No horizontal scaling story: The architecture assumes a single Python process.

docs.title: 8.3 Security
docs.text:
• Dynamic execution risk: register_tool sandbox is good but not bulletproof. Consider WebAssembly (Wasmtime) or seccomp-bpf for stronger isolation.
  • Secret management: API keys in JSON config file; consider integration with OS keyrings or external secret managers.
  • No CSP headers: Web UI may be vulnerable to XSS if user-generated content is rendered.

docs.title: 8.4 Maintainability
docs.text:
• Large files: agent.py (71KB), provider.py (53KB), toolbox.py (41KB) exceed comfortable single-file complexity thresholds.
  • Mixed async patterns: Some modules use asyncio.to_thread, others use aiosqlite, others use dedicated thread pools. A unified concurrency strategy would help.
  • Test duplication: Some sprint integration tests may overlap with unit tests.

docs.title: 8.5 Missing Features
docs.text:
• Slack channel adapter: Mentioned in optional deps but not yet implemented.
  • Enterprise RBAC: Basic scopes exist but no fine-grained resource-level permissions.
  • LoRA adapter loading: Mentioned in roadmap but not present.
  • Agent internals DI: Roadmap mentions explicit dependency injection.

  3. Implement WebAssembly sandbox for register_tool as an optional high-security mode
  4. Add load testing with locust or k6 to identify SQLite concurrency bottlenecks
  5. Add CSP and security headers middleware to api_server.py

1. Horizontal scaling: Message bus (Redis/RabbitMQ) for multi-process agent swarms
  2. Enterprise RBAC: Resource-level permissions with audit logging
  3. Model serving: Integrate vLLM/TGI for self-hosted model inference
  4. Formal verification: Consider TLA+ or similar for the circuit breaker and fallback chain state machines

docs.title: ZenSynora — Optimization & Improvement Audit
docs.text:
Archived on 2026-10-13 (v0.7.0). Optimization audit. Kept for history; it describes the project at the time it was written and may not match the current code. Current documentation: docs/README.md.

Generated: 2026-05-17 Scope: Full codebase (myclaw/, webui/, tooling, config) Method: Targeted file inspection across agent.py, provider.py, memory.py, knowledge/db.py, config.py, defaults.py, tools/shell.py, deploy.py, async_scheduler.py, agent_internals/classes.py, task_timer.py, .pre-commit-config.yaml, and related modules

docs.title: 1. deploy.py — Hardcoded SSH credentials committed to source tree
docs.text:
File: deploy.py, lines 23–26

REMOTE_HOST = "192.168.8.110"
REMOTE_USER = "adi"
REMOTE_PASS = "<redacted>"
REMOTE_DIR  = "/home/adi/zensynora"

Plaintext SSH password and host are committed. Anyone with repo access gets live credentials.

Fix: Replace literals with environment variable reads:

REMOTE_HOST = os.environ.get("ZENSYNORA_DEPLOY_HOST", "")
REMOTE_USER = os.environ.get("ZENSYNORA_DEPLOY_USER", "")
REMOTE_PASS = os.environ.get("ZENSYNORA_DEPLOY_PASS", "")
REMOTE_DIR  = os.environ.get("ZENSYNORA_DEPLOY_DIR", "/home/adi/zensynora")

Add a pre-commit hook that scans for = "..." / = '...' patterns on credential-named variables.

docs.title: 2. memory.py — Unbounded _history_cache can OOM on long sessions
docs.text:
File: myclaw/memory.py, ~line 466

Memory._history_cache is a plain dict keyed by limit (an integer). Every distinct limit value ever requested becomes a permanent cache entry. A session calling get_history(limit=10) then limit=20 then limit=50 accumulates entries without bound. The _cache_max_size cap uses a simple FIFO eviction that only fires for the default-columns path:

if len(self._history_cache) >= self._cache_max_size:
    oldest_key = next(iter(self._history_cache))
    del self._history_cache[oldest_key]

This evicts one entry per overflow call — but never shrinks below the cap, and non-default column queries bypass the cap entirely.

Fix: Replace with collections.OrderedDict with a strict max-length policy, or use cachetools.LRUCache:

from collections import OrderedDict
self._history_cache: OrderedDict[int, list] = OrderedDict()
# On every put:
self._history_cache[cache_key] = result
self._history_cache.move_to_end(cache_key)
if len(self._history_cache) > self._cache_max_size:
    self._history_cache.popitem(last=False)

Also: the sub-query SELECT ... FROM (SELECT ... ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?) ORDER BY id ASC forces SQLite to materialize a full reverse-sorted set before reversing. A primary-key scan ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ? followed by in-Python reversal is cheaper for small limit values.

docs.title: 3. asyncio.create_task without exception guards — silent crashes at 27 call sites
docs.text:
Files across: agent.py, skill_preloader.py, messaging/broker.py, agent_internals/tool_executor.py, agent_internals/context_builder.py, agent_internals/classes.py, worker_pool.py, gateway.py, mcp/client.py, async_scheduler.py, agents/medic_change_mgmt.py, tools/scheduler.py, task_timer.py, swarm/orchestrator.py, swarm/collaboration.py, swarm/storage.py, knowledge/sync.py

27 fire-and-forget asyncio.create_task() / loop.create_task() calls exist. None attach a .add_done_callback that logs exceptions. If a background coroutine raises, the asyncio event loop either logs "Task exception was never retrieved" at shutdown (development) or silently discards the error (production with loop.set_exception_handler suppressed).

Worst offenders: - agent.py lines 1608, 1615 — _extract_and_save_knowledge and _background_summarize_context (LLM calls that can raise silently) - agent_internals/classes.py lines 201, 222 — same KB/summarization tasks - knowledge/sync.py lines 349, 356, 360 — background file-watcher extraction tasks

Fix: Apply a module-level helper:

def _fire_and_forget(coro, logger, context=""):
    task = asyncio.create_task(coro)
    task.add_done_callback(
        lambda t: logger.error(f"Bg task failed [{context}]", exc_info=t.exception())
        if t.exception() else None
    )
    return task

Then replace every raw asyncio.create_task(coro) with _fire_and_forget(coro, logger, "context-name").

docs.title: 4. re module recompiled inside hot loops in 11+ files
docs.text:
Files: agent.py, shell.py, memory.py, web_search.py, benchmark_runner.py, agents/medic_evolver.py, agents/medic_change_mgmt.py, backends/router.py, self_healer.py, skill_generator.py, agents/skill_adapter.py, sandbox.py

Several files compile regex inline on every call instead of once at module scope:

  • agent.py line 796: re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", " ", ...) on every think() call
  • shell.py line 52: re.compile(r"[\n\r;&|$(){}[]\]")once pershell_async()` call
  • memory.py: re.findall(pattern, text) with uncompiled pattern strings in extract_knowledge_candidates

Fix: Module-level compiled constants:

# agent.py
_TOPIC_SANITIZE_RE = re.compile(r"[^\w\s]")

# shell.py
_DANGEROUS_CHARS_RE = re.compile(r"[\n\r;&|`$(){}\[\]\\]")

# memory.py
_ENTITY_PATTERNS_COMPILED = [re.compile(p) for p in ENTITY_PATTERNS]

docs.title: 5. agent.py still 1,630 lines — class decomposition in agent_internals/classes.py exists but is unused
docs.text:
Sprint 5 extracted 4 free functions; Sprint 9 wrapped them in thin class adapters (MessageRouter, ContextBuilder, ToolExecutor, ResponseHandler). agent.py still imports and calls the free functions directly. The class layer was built for DI/testability but Agent was never migrated to it.

Migrating Agent._route_message → MessageRouter.run(), _build_context → ContextBuilder.run(), _execute_tools → ToolExecutor.run() would cut agent.py by an estimated 40–50% and give every phase an explicit dependency surface for testing.

docs.title: 6. Semantic cache manual np.dot loop — 5–15× slower than batched matmul
docs.text:
File: myclaw/vector/semantic_cache.py (or equivalent semantic cache module)

The embedding scan iterates over every cached entry individually:

for entry in cache.values():
    score = np.dot(query_vec, entry.embedding)   # O(N) BLAS calls

Fix: Stack embeddings into a single matrix and call np.matmul once:

embeddings = np.stack([e.embedding for e in cache.values()])   # shape (N, dim)
scores = query_vec @ embeddings.T                               # single BLAS call
top_k = np.argpartition(scores, -k)[-k:]

Also: scan_cap defaults to 64. With a typical cache of 256 entries only 25% are ever scored. Raising the cap to 256 or adding an L2-distance pre-filter (cheap approximate nearest-neighbors) before the dot-product pass would materially improve retrieval quality.

docs.title: 7. Topic extraction uses re.sub on every think() call — replace with str.translate
docs.text:
File: myclaw/agent.py, line 796

cleaned = re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", " ", message.lower())

This runs on every user message and recompiles the pattern each invocation. str.translate with a pre-built translation table runs in C and avoids the regex engine entirely:

# module scope
_TOPIC_TABLE = str.maketrans(
    {chr(c): " " for c in range(128) if not (chr(c).isalnum() or chr(c).isspace())}
)
# per call
cleaned = message.lower().translate(_TOPIC_TABLE)

docs.title: 8. Per-user DB pool fragments SQLite write throughput
docs.text:
File: myclaw/memory.py, AsyncSQLitePool

Memory() creates a separate AsyncSQLitePool (3 connections) per user_id.db. Ten active users = 30 connection slots across 10 files. SQLite's WAL writer serializes at the filesystem level, so per-file pool concurrency does not help writes — it only adds connection-table overhead. The per-user read isolation is sound, but the pool size of 3 per DB is over-provisioned for write-heavy workloads.

Fix: Limit each pool to 1 connection for writes, 2 for reads. Detect workload type and resize accordingly.

docs.title: 9. _history_cache not thread-safe across sync/async paths
docs.text:
File: myclaw/memory.py

Memory._history_cache is a plain dict mutated from get_history (async/event-loop path) and from close() / cleanup() which can be called via asyncio.to_thread. The GIL serializes single opcodes but dict resizes are not atomic under asyncio.to_thread. In practice rare, but a threading.Lock on the cache mutations would eliminate the race.

docs.title: 10. AsyncScheduler JSONL persistence has no file lock
docs.text:
File: myclaw/async_scheduler.py

Jobs are persisted to ~/.myclaw/async_scheduler_jobs.jsonl with no fcntl/msvcrt advisory lock. If two scheduler instances start simultaneously (e.g., systemd Restart=on-failure races two starts), the JSONL can be interleaved and corrupted.

Fix: Wrap the JSONL file in an fcntl.flock context manager on both read and write paths.

docs.title: 11. Shell regex duplicated between sync and async functions
docs.text:
File: myclaw/tools/shell.py, lines 52 and 137

Both shell_async() and shell() compile the same dangerous regex on every call. Extract to a module-level constant:

_DANGEROUS_CHARS_RE = re.compile(r"[\n\r;&|`$(){}\[\]\\]")

docs.title: 12. LRUCacheWithTTL._cleanup_expired is O(n) on every Nth access
docs.text:
File: myclaw/provider.py, LRUCacheWithTTL

_cleanup_expired rebuilds a list of all expired keys and deletes them in a loop. Called amortized on every N accesses, it is fine for maxsize=128 but stalls for maxsize=1000+ (possible with semantic_cache at scale). Make it lazy — only clean the specific expired key on .get() miss, or run a background cleanup task.

docs.title: 14. config.py _apply_env_overrides — secrets silently accepted with no startup warning
docs.text:
File: myclaw/config.py, line 212

Environment variable names are logged at INFO level; values are not. That is correct. However, save_config writes plaintext secrets to config.json when no encryption key is configured, with no warning. If the operator enables MYCLAW_SQLITE_KEY after saving plaintext, a stale unencrypted config.json remains on disk.

Fix: Log a WARNING on first call to save_config when encryption is not active and secrets are present.

docs.title: 15. CORS fallback to dev origin not guarded against empty configuration
docs.text:
File: myclaw/web/api.py, line 82

_cors_origins = _cors_origins.cors_origins if _cors_origins else ["http://localhost:5173"]

If security.cors_origins is set to [] (empty list) the fallback kicks in to dev-only. If it accidently contains "*" the CORS middleware allows any origin with credentials — a known class of attack (any site can steal sessions). Add an explicit validation in _validate_config:

if "*" in config.security.cors_origins:
    logger.warning("CORS wildcard with credentials is a security risk")

docs.title: 16. stream_think word-splitting corrupts markdown / multi-byte output
docs.text:
File: myclaw/agent.py

words = final_response.split(" ")
for i, word in enumerate(words):
    prefix = " " if i > 0 else ""
    yield prefix + word

Splitting on ASCII space breaks code blocks, tables, and multi-byte Unicode strings. If final_response contains backtick-delimited code, "```" becomes a separate token, breaking the stream consumer's reconstruction. Use a fixed-size chunk strategy (e.g., 8-character windows with overlap) or stream the full string per character instead of word-splitting.

docs.title: 17. requirements.txt absent; requirements-lock.txt underutilized
docs.text: The project ships requirements-lock.txt (14 entries, core only). install.sh ignores it and installs from pyproject.toml editable. The Dockerfile installs from requirements.txt but the file does not exist — it silently falls through elsewhere. Generate a fully-pinned requirements.txt from the existing uv.lock and have both install.sh and CI use it to pin environments.

docs.title: 18. No .env / pydantic-settings schema validation
docs.text: .env.example documents 50+ variables without types. The app reads them via os.environ.get + manual Pydantic overrides in config.py. Mistyped environment variable names are silently ignored, producing default values at runtime. Adding pydantic-settings BaseSettings with explicit field types and a startup validation pass would surface misconfigurations with a clear error before the agent starts.

docs.title: 19. Ruff + Black competing in pre-commit config
docs.text:
File: .pre-commit-config.yaml

Both ruff-format and black are configured as formatters. Running both can silently undo each other's formatting — Ruff formats one way, Black reformats on the next hook, or vice-versa. Use one formatter:

  • Recommended: Remove black and keep ruff-format — it is faster and already configured.
  • Alternative: Remove ruff-format and keep black, but run ruff (linter-only, not ruff-format).

docs.title: 2. Code Structure & Modularity
docs.text: Area Observation Recommendation Status myclaw/agent/ contains many small modules that each import most of the same heavy utilities. Repeated imports increase import time and memory footprint. Create a shared myclaw/agent/_common.py or consolidate into agent_internals/. ⚠️ Partially — agent refactored to agent.py + agent_internals/ Circular imports Can cause runtime import errors and hide bugs. Refactor to lazy-load where possible or restructure the package to break the cycle. ⚠️ Partially — TYPE_CHECKING guards used throughout Multiple entry points perform overlapping setups (logging, config loading). Duplication leads to drift and harder maintenance. Centralize bootstrapping in a single helper. ✅ Resolved — init_app() in myclaw/__init__.py (2026-05-17)

docs.title: 3. Performance Hotspots
docs.text: File / Function Hot path Optimisation Status myclaw/worker_pool.py — task polling loop Busy-wait consumes CPU cycles under load. Switch to queue-based blocking. ✅ Already fixed — uses asyncio.PriorityQueue + await queue.get() myclaw/context_window.py — string concatenation O(n^2) string building for large histories. Use list accumulation and ''.join(). ✅ Already fixed — uses list comprehension + join myclaw/mcp/client.py — HTTP calls Each call creates a new TCP connection. Adopt a single requests.Session per client. ✅ Already fixed — http_session.py provides shared session Tests spin up full server for unit tests. Overly heavyweight; slows CI. Mock network layer; reserve full server for integration subset. ⚠️ Open

docs.title: 4. Asynchronous / Concurrency
docs.text: Observation Impact Fix Status Mixed sync/async code Event-loop recreation overhead and potential deadlocks. Define a top-level async entry point. ✅ Already fixed — agent_internals/router.py is fully async No explicit rate-limiting on external tool calls. Potential throttling by APIs leading to failures. Add a token-bucket limiter around tool calls. ✅ Resolved — RateLimiter in tools/core.py + web search rate limits (2026-05-18)

docs.title: 5. Logging & Error Handling
docs.text: Issue Recommendation Status Logging configuration is scattered; modules call basicConfig directly. Centralised logger (myclaw/logging_config.py) with consistent formatter. ✅ Resolved — logging.py deprecated in favor of logging_config.py (2026-05-18) Exceptions are sometimes swallowed (except Exception: pass). Preserve stack traces or re-raise with context. ⚠️ Open docs/exception_handling_implementation.md outlines a design not fully reflected in code. Align implementation with the documented pattern. ⚠️ Open

docs.title: 6. Testing & Coverage
docs.text: Observation Action Status Several integration tests are flaky on Windows. Add platform guards or pytest.mark.xfail with clear rationale. ✅ Resolved (2026-05-17) No coverage badge or CI enforcement. Integrate pytest-cov into CI. ✅ Resolved — --cov-fail-under=60 in pyproject.toml (2026-05-18) Concurrency tests rely on time.sleep for synchronization. Replace with Event, Barrier for determinism. ✅ Resolved (2026-05-18)

docs.title: 7. Security
docs.text: Area Issue Remedy Status config_encryption.py reads encryption keys from environment variables without validation. Missing fallback could expose plaintext configs. Validate key length/format and raise a clear error if absent. ✅ Resolved — Fernet key format validation (2026-05-17) myclaw/web_search.py constructs URLs by simple string interpolation. Potential URL injection. Use urllib.parse.urljoin and urllib.parse.quote_plus. ✅ Resolved (2026-05-17) No static analysis step in pre-commit. Vulnerabilities may slip in. Add bandit and safety. ✅ Resolved (2026-05-17) API key comparison uses direct string equality. Vulnerable to timing attacks. Use secrets.compare_digest(). ✅ Resolved — web/auth.py (2026-05-18) XML parsing vulnerable to billion-laughs attacks. DoS via entity expansion. Use defusedxml with fallback. ✅ Resolved — web_search.py (2026-05-18)

docs.title: 8. Documentation & Onboarding
docs.text: Issue Recommendation Status Multiple out-of-date docs vs actual code. Periodically generate documentation from source or add Docs Review todo. ✅ Resolved — docs/review01.md created (2026-05-17), OPTIMIZATION_RECOMMENDATIONS.md updated (2026-05-18) README.md lacks quick-start commands for the new worker-pool model. Add a short "Running locally" block. ✅ Resolved — README updated (2026-05-18)
